bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第054卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 54.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 54.

sentences.zh: 【漢紀四十六】　起強圉作噩，盡昭陽單閼，凡七年。

translations.literal: 【Han Records 46】 From Qiangyu Zuoe through Zhaoyang Danyan—in all, seven years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Han Records 46】 From the first year of the Qiangyu cycle through the last year of the Zhaoyang cycle—seven years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己未，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day jiwei, there was an amnesty for all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on jiwei day, an amnesty was proclaimed for the empire.

sentences.zh: 居風令貪暴無度，縣人朱達等與蠻夷同反，攻殺令，聚眾至四五千人。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Jufeng was greedy and violent without measure; the county men Zhu Da and others joined with the Man and Yi in rebellion, attacked and killed the magistrate, and gathered a host of four or five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Jufeng was greedily violent beyond measure. Zhu Da and others of the county joined Man and Yi tribesmen in revolt, killed the magistrate, and rallied a force of four or five thousand.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，進攻九真，九真太守兒式戰死。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, they advanced to attack Jiuzhen; the Administrator of Jiuzhen, Ni Shi, died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the rebels advanced on Jiuzhen; Nine Gates Administrator Ni Shi was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 詔九真都尉魏朗討破之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Commandant of Jiuzhen, Wei Lang, to campaign against them and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Jiuzhen Commandant Wei Lang to campaign against them and defeat them.

sentences.zh: 閏月，庚辰晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the last day of the cycle gengchen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the last day of gengchen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 京師蝗。

translations.literal: Locusts plagued the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts plagued the capital.

sentences.zh: 或上言：「民之貧困以貨輕錢薄，宜改鑄大錢。

translations.literal: Someone submitted a memorial saying: "The people's poverty is due to the lightness of goods and thinness of coin; it is fitting to recast large coins."
translations.idiomatic: Someone submitted a memorial saying, "The people's poverty stems from light goods and thin coinage; large coins should be recast."

sentences.zh: 」事下四府群僚及太學能言之士議之。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the four offices' assembled officials and eloquent men of the Imperial University for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was referred to the four offices' assembled officials and eloquent scholars of the Imperial University for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 太學生劉陶上議曰：「當今之憂，不在於貨，在乎民饑。

translations.literal: Imperial University student Liu Tao submitted a proposal, saying: "The present worry is not in goods but in the people's hunger."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial University student Liu Tao submitted a proposal, saying, "The present worry is not in goods but in the people's hunger."

sentences.zh: 竊見比年已來，良苗盡於蝗螟之口，杼軸空於公私之求。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that in recent years good seedlings have all been consumed by locusts and caterpillars, and looms stand empty under demands public and private.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has observed that in recent years good seedlings have all been consumed by locusts and caterpillars, and looms stand empty under demands public and private.

sentences.zh: 民所患者，豈謂錢貨之厚薄，銖兩之輕重哉！

translations.literal: What the people suffer from—how could it be said to be the thickness or thinness of money, the weight of tael and ounce!
translations.idiomatic: What the people suffer from—how could it be the thickness or thinness of money, the weight of tael and ounce!

sentences.zh: 就使當今沙礫化為南金，瓦石變為和玉，使百姓渴無所飲，饑無所食，雖皇、羲之純德，唐、虞之文明，猶不能以保蕭牆之內也。

translations.literal: Even if today gravel were transformed into southern gold and tiles and stones into hehe jade, yet the common people had nowhere to drink when thirsty and nothing to eat when hungry—even the pure virtue of Huangdi and Fuxi and the civilization of Tang and Yu could not preserve peace within the palace walls.
translations.idiomatic: Even if today gravel were transformed into southern gold and tiles and stones into hehe jade, yet the common people had nowhere to drink when thirsty and nothing to eat when hungry—even the pure virtue of Huangdi and Fuxi and the civilization of Tang and Yu could not preserve peace within the palace walls.

sentences.zh: 蓋民可百年無貨，不可一朝有饑，故食為至急也。

translations.literal: For the people can go a hundred years without goods but cannot endure a single morning of hunger; therefore food is the utmost urgency.
translations.idiomatic: For the people can go a hundred years without goods but cannot endure a single morning of hunger; therefore food is the utmost urgency.

sentences.zh: 議者不達農殖之本，多言鑄冶之便。

translations.literal: Those who debate do not reach to the root of farming and cultivation but speak much of the convenience of casting and smelting.
translations.idiomatic: Those who debate do not reach to the root of farming and cultivation but speak much of the convenience of casting and smelting.

sentences.zh: 蓋萬人鑄之，一人奪之，猶不能給；

translations.literal: If ten thousand men cast and one man seizes, still it cannot suffice;
translations.idiomatic: If ten thousand men cast and one man seizes, still it cannot suffice;

sentences.zh: 況今一人鑄之，則萬人奪之乎！

translations.literal: how much less when today one man casts and then ten thousand men seize!
translations.idiomatic: how much less when today one man casts and then ten thousand men seize!

sentences.zh: 雖以陰陽為炭，萬物為銅，役不食之民，使不饑之士，猶不能足無厭之求也。

translations.literal: Even using yin and yang as charcoal and the myriad things as copper, employing men who do not eat and making men who are not hungry—still one cannot satisfy insatiable demands.
translations.idiomatic: Even using yin and yang as charcoal and the myriad things as copper, employing men who do not eat and making men who are not hungry—still one cannot satisfy insatiable demands.

sentences.zh: 夫欲民殷財阜，要在止役禁奪，則百姓不勞而足。

translations.literal: If one wishes the people prosperous and wealth abundant, the key lies in stopping corvée labor and forbidding seizure—then the hundred surnames will be sufficient without toil.
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes the people prosperous and wealth abundant, the key lies in stopping corvée labor and forbidding seizure—then the hundred surnames will be sufficient without toil.

sentences.zh: 陛下愍海內之憂戚，欲鑄錢齊貨以救其弊，猶養魚沸鼎之中。

translations.literal: Your Majesty pities the grief and distress within the seas and wishes to cast coin to equalize goods to save its ills—it is like raising fish in a boiling cauldron
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pities the grief and distress within the seas and wishes to cast coin to equalize goods to save its ills—it is like raising fish in a boiling cauldron

sentences.zh: 棲鳥烈火之上；

translations.literal: and nesting birds upon blazing fire;
translations.idiomatic: and nesting birds upon blazing fire;

sentences.zh: 水、木，本魚鳥之所生也，用之不時，必至焦爛。

translations.literal: water and wood are what fish and birds are born from, yet used at the wrong time they must be scorched and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: water and wood are what fish and birds are born from, yet used at the wrong time they must be scorched and ruined.

sentences.zh: 願陛下寬鍥薄之禁，後冶鑄之議，聽民庶之謠吟，問路叟之所憂，瞰三光之文耀，視山河之分流，天下之心，國家大事，粲然皆見，無有遺惑者矣。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to relax harsh prohibitions on coinage, defer deliberation on smelting and casting, heed the ballads of the people, ask what old men on the road worry over, survey the splendor of the three luminaries and view the branching of mountains and rivers—the mind of all under heaven and the great affairs of state will all stand forth clear, with nothing left obscure.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to relax harsh prohibitions on coinage, defer deliberation on smelting and casting, heed the ballads of the people, ask what old men on the road worry over, survey the splendor of the three luminaries and view the branching of mountains and rivers—the mind of all under heaven and the great affairs of state will all stand forth clear, with nothing left obscure.

sentences.zh: 伏念當今地廣而不得耕，民眾而無所食，群小競進，秉國之位，鷹揚天下，鳥鈔求飽，吞肌及骨，並噬無厭。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that today the land is broad yet cannot be tilled, the people are many yet have nothing to eat; petty men compete to advance, holding the state's positions, hawk-like over all under heaven, plundering to fill their bellies, devouring flesh to the bone, swallowing together without satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant reflects that today the land is broad yet cannot be tilled, the people are many yet have nothing to eat; petty men compete to advance, holding the state's positions, hawk-like over all under heaven, plundering to fill their bellies, devouring flesh to the bone, swallowing together without satiety.

sentences.zh: 誠恐卒有役夫、窮匠起於板築之間，投斤攘臂，登高遠呼，使怨之民響應雲合。

translations.literal: Your servant truly fears that suddenly corvée laborers and destitute artisans may rise from among the rammed-earth workers, seize axes and fling up their arms, climb high and shout far, and make resentful people answer like clouds gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant truly fears that suddenly corvée laborers and destitute artisans may rise from among the rammed-earth workers, seize axes and fling up their arms, climb high and shout far, and make resentful people answer like clouds gathering.

sentences.zh: 雖方尺之錢，何有能救其危也！

translations.literal: Even square-foot coins—what could save their peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Even square-foot coins—what could save their peril!"

sentences.zh: 」遂不改錢。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the coinage was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the coinage was not changed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，司徒尹頌薨。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Minister of Works Yin Song died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the eleventh month, Minister of Works Yin Song died.

sentences.zh: 長沙蠻反，寇益陽。

translations.literal: The Man of Changsha rebelled and raided Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Man of Changsha rebelled and raided Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 以司空韓縯為司徒，以太常北海孫朗為司空。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works Han Yan was made Minister over the Masses, and Grand Minister of Ceremonies Sun Lang of Beihai was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Han Yan was appointed Minister over the Masses, and Grand Minister of Ceremonies Sun Lang of Beihai was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，甲戊晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the last day of the cycle jiaxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on the last day of jiaxu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 太史令陳授因小黃門徐璜陳「日食之變咎在大將軍冀」。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Chen Shou, through the junior yellow gate attendant Xu Huang, presented that "the eclipse's blame lies with the Grand General Ji."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Chen Shou, through junior yellow gate attendant Xu Huang, presented that "the eclipse's blame lies with Grand General Ji."

sentences.zh: 冀聞之，諷雒陽收考授，死於獄。

translations.literal: When Ji heard of it, he prompted Luoyang to arrest and examine Shou; Shou died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji heard of it, he prompted Luoyang to arrest and examine Shou; Shou died in prison.

sentences.zh: 帝由是怒冀。

translations.literal: Because of this the Emperor grew angry with Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the Emperor grew angry with Ji.

sentences.zh: 京師蝗。

translations.literal: Locusts plagued the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts plagued the capital.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊寅，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day wuyin, there was an amnesty for all under heaven and the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuyin day, an amnesty was proclaimed for the empire and the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 大雩。

translations.literal: A great rain prayer was performed.
translations.idiomatic: A great rain prayer was performed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲子，太尉黃瓊免；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jiazi, Grand Commandant Huang Qiong was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jiazi day, Grand Commandant Huang Qiong was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 以太常胡廣為太尉。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Ceremonies Hu Guang was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Ceremonies Hu Guang was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，帝校獵廣成，遂幸上林苑。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Emperor conducted a hunt at Guangcheng and then visited the Shanglin Park.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, the Emperor conducted a hunt at Guangcheng and then visited the Shanglin Park.

sentences.zh: 十二月，南匈奴諸部並叛，與烏桓、鮮卑寇緣邊九郡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the various divisions of the Southern Xiongnu all rebelled and, with the Wuhuan and Xianbei, raided nine commanderies along the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, the various divisions of the Southern Xiongnu all rebelled and, with the Wuhuan and Xianbei, raided nine commanderies along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝以京兆尹陳龜為度遼將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Metropolitan Governor Chen Gui General Who Crosses the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor appointed Metropolitan Governor Chen Gui General Who Crosses the Liao.

sentences.zh: 龜臨行，上疏曰：「臣聞三辰不軌，擢士為相；

translations.literal: As Gui was about to depart, he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that when the three luminaries are irregular, one promotes a scholar to be chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: As Gui was about to depart, he submitted a memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that when the three luminaries are irregular, one promotes a scholar to be chancellor;

sentences.zh: 蠻夷不恭，拔卒為將。

translations.literal: when the Man and Yi are not respectful, one selects a soldier to be general.
translations.idiomatic: when the Man and Yi are not respectful, one selects a soldier to be general.

sentences.zh: 臣無文武之才，而忝鷹揚之任，雖歿軀體，無所云補。

translations.literal: Your servant has no civil or martial talent yet disgracefully bears the hawk-displaying commission; though I die in body, there is nothing to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has no civil or martial talent yet disgracefully bears the hawk-displaying commission; though I die in body, there is nothing to repay.

sentences.zh: 今西州邊鄙，土地□脊□角，民數更寇虜，室家殘破，雖含生氣，實同枯朽。

translations.literal: Now the western provinces' frontier marches—the land is barren and rugged; the people have repeatedly suffered the bandits; households are shattered; though they contain breath of life, they are in truth like dry rot.
translations.idiomatic: Now the western provinces' frontier marches—the land is barren and rugged; the people have repeatedly suffered the bandits; households are shattered; though they contain breath of life, they are in truth like dry rot.

sentences.zh: 往歲并州水雨，災螟互生，稼穡荒耗，租更空闕。

translations.literal: In past years Bing province had floods and rain; disasters of locusts and caterpillars arose together; crops were wasted and exhausted; land tax and corvée were empty and lacking.
translations.idiomatic: In past years Bing province had floods and rain; disasters of locusts and caterpillars arose together; crops were wasted and exhausted; land tax and corvée were empty and lacking.

sentences.zh: 陛下以百姓為子，焉可不垂撫循之恩哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty takes the hundred surnames as children—how can you not bestow comforting and nurturing grace!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty takes the hundred surnames as children—how can you not bestow comforting and nurturing grace!

sentences.zh: 古公、西伯天下歸仁，豈復輿金輦寶以為民惠乎！

translations.literal: The ancient duke and the Earl of the West won the realm's allegiance by benevolence—did they again carry gold and jade in carriages to be the people's bounty!
translations.idiomatic: The ancient duke and the Earl of the West won the realm's allegiance by benevolence—did they again carry gold and jade in carriages to be the people's bounty!

sentences.zh: 陛下繼中興之統，承光武之業，臨朝聽政而未留聖意。

translations.literal: Your Majesty succeeds the Restoration line and inherits Guangwu's enterprise, yet in holding court and hearing government you have not yet fixed your sage intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty succeeds the Restoration line and inherits Guangwu's enterprise, yet in holding court and hearing government you have not yet fixed your sage intent.

sentences.zh: 且牧守不良，或出中官，懼逆上旨，取過目前。

translations.literal: Moreover governors and prefects are not good; some issue from palace eunuchs; fearing to go against the superior's intent, they take only what passes before the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover governors and prefects are not good; some issue from palace eunuchs; fearing to go against the superior's intent, they take only what passes before the eyes.

sentences.zh: 呼嗟之聲，招致災害，胡虜凶悍，因衰緣隙；

translations.literal: The sound of sighing summons disaster; the Hu and Rong are fierce and seize upon decline through gaps;
translations.idiomatic: The sound of sighing summons disaster; the Hu and Rong are fierce and seize upon decline through gaps;

sentences.zh: 而令倉庫單于豺狼之口，功業無銖兩之效，皆由將帥不忠，聚奸所致。

translations.literal: yet the treasuries enrich the mouths of wolves, achievements have not a tael's effect—all because generals are not loyal and wicked men gather.
translations.idiomatic: yet the treasuries enrich the mouths of wolves, achievements have not a tael's effect—all because generals are not loyal and wicked men gather.

sentences.zh: 前涼州刺史祝良，初除到州，多所糾罰，太守令長，貶黜將半，政未逾時，功效卓然，實應賞異，以勸功能；

translations.literal: Formerly Liangzhou Inspector Zhu Liang, when first appointed and arrived at the province, imposed many corrections and punishments; prefects and magistrates, demoted and dismissed, were nearly half; government had not passed its season yet achievements stood forth—truly he should have been rewarded exceptionally to encourage merit;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Liangzhou Inspector Zhu Liang, when first appointed and arrived at the province, imposed many corrections and punishments; prefects and magistrates, demoted and dismissed, were nearly half; government had not passed its season yet achievements stood forth—truly he should have been rewarded exceptionally to encourage merit;

sentences.zh: 改任牧守，去斥奸殘；

translations.literal: change and appoint governors and prefects, remove and expel the wicked and cruel;
translations.idiomatic: change and appoint governors and prefects, remove and expel the wicked and cruel;

sentences.zh: 又宜更選匈奴、烏桓護羌中郎將、校尉，簡練文下，授之法令；

translations.literal: again it is fitting to newly select the Protector of the Qiang, the Wuhuan and Xiongnu Commandants, and the Colonel—choose and refine civil and military men, confer upon them laws and ordinances;
translations.idiomatic: again it is fitting to newly select the Protector of the Qiang, the Wuhuan and Xiongnu Commandants, and the Colonel—choose and refine civil and military men, confer upon them laws and ordinances;

sentences.zh: 除並、涼二州今年租、更，寬赦罪隸，掃除更始。

translations.literal: remit this year's land tax and corvée for Bing and Liang provinces, broadly pardon criminals and bondsmen, sweep away and make a new beginning.
translations.idiomatic: remit this year's land tax and corvée for Bing and Liang provinces, broadly pardon criminals and bondsmen, sweep away and make a new beginning.

sentences.zh: 則善吏知奉公之祐，惡者覺營私之禍，胡馬可不窺長城，塞下無候望之患矣。

translations.literal: Then good officials will know the blessing of serving the public, and the wicked will feel the calamity of seeking private gain; Hu horses may not peer at the Long Wall, and below the passes there will be no worry of watch and lookout."
translations.idiomatic: Then good officials will know the blessing of serving the public, and the wicked will feel the calamity of seeking private gain; Hu horses may not peer at the Long Wall, and below the passes there will be no worry of watch and lookout."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃更選幽、并刺史，自營、郡太守、都尉以下，多所革易。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon newly selected the inspectors of You and Bing; from colonels, commandery administrators, commandants, and below, many were replaced.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor thereupon newly selected the inspectors of You and Bing; from colonels, commandery administrators, commandants, and below, many were replaced.

sentences.zh: 下詔為陳將軍除並、涼一年租賦，以賜吏民。

translations.literal: An edict remitted one year's land tax and corvée for Bing and Liang on behalf of General Chen and bestowed them on officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: An edict remitted one year's land tax and corvée for Bing and Liang on behalf of General Chen and bestowed them on officials and people.

sentences.zh: 龜到職，州郡重足震慄，省息經用，歲以億計。

translations.literal: When Gui arrived on duty, the provinces and commanderies stood in awe trembling, economized routine expenses, and saved hundreds of millions each year.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui arrived on duty, the provinces and commanderies stood in awe trembling, economized routine expenses, and saved hundreds of millions each year.

sentences.zh: 詔拜安定屬國都尉張奐為北中郎將，以討匈奴、烏桓等。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Commandant of the Dependent State of Anding Zhang Huan North Colonel; to campaign against the Xiongnu, Wuhuan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Commandant of the Dependent State of Anding Zhang Huan North Colonel to campaign against the Xiongnu, Wuhuan, and others.

sentences.zh: 匈奴、烏桓燒度遼將軍門，引屯赤阬，煙火相望。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu and Wuhuan burned the gate of the General Who Crosses the Liao, drew off and encamped at Red Pit; beacon fires faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu and Wuhuan burned the gate of the General Who Crosses the Liao, drew off and encamped at Red Pit; beacon fires faced one another.

sentences.zh: 兵眾大恐，各欲亡去。

translations.literal: The troops were greatly afraid; each wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were greatly afraid; each wished to flee.

sentences.zh: 奐安坐帷中，與弟子講誦自若，軍士稍安。

translations.literal: Huan sat calmly within the curtain lecturing and reciting with his disciples as if at ease; the soldiers gradually grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: Huan sat calmly within the curtain lecturing and reciting with his disciples as if at ease; the soldiers gradually grew calm.

sentences.zh: 乃潛誘烏桓，陰與和通，遂使斬匈奴、屠各渠帥，襲破其眾，諸胡悉降。

translations.literal: Then he secretly enticed the Wuhuan, secretly made peace with them, and had them behead the Xiongnu and Tuge chieftains, surprise-attack and break their host; all the Hu submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Then he secretly enticed the Wuhuan, secretly made peace with them, and had them behead the Xiongnu and Tuge chieftains, surprise-attack and break their host; all the Hu submitted.

sentences.zh: 奐以南單于車兒不能統理國事，乃拘之，奏立左谷蠡王為單于。

translations.literal: Huan, because the Southern Chanyu Che'er could not govern the state's affairs, detained him and memorialized to establish the Left Guli King as chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan, because the Southern Chanyu Che'er could not govern the state's affairs, detained him and memorialized to establish the Left Guli King as chanyu.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「《春秋》大居正；

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Spring and Annals greatly honor the correct succession;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The Spring and Annals greatly honor the correct succession;

sentences.zh: 車兒一心向化，何罪而黜！

translations.literal: Che'er with one heart turned to transformation—what crime to dismiss!
translations.idiomatic: Che'er with one heart turned to transformation—what crime to dismiss!

sentences.zh: 其遣還庭！

translations.literal: Send him back to the court!"
translations.idiomatic: Send him back to the court!"

sentences.zh: 大將軍冀與陳龜素有隙，譖其沮毀國威，挑取功譽，不為胡虜所畏，坐征還，以種暠為度遼將軍。

translations.literal: Grand General Ji and Chen Gui had long borne a grudge; he slandered Gui for discouraging and ruining the state's prestige and picking out merit for glory, not being feared by the Hu and Rong; Gui was summoned back on that charge, and Chong Hao was made General Who Crosses the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Ji and Chen Gui had long borne a grudge; he slandered Gui for discouraging and ruining the state's prestige and picking out merit for glory, not being feared by the Hu and Rong; Gui was summoned back on that charge, and Chong Hao was made General Who Crosses the Liao.

sentences.zh: 龜遂乞骸骨歸田裡，復征為尚書。

translations.literal: Gui thereupon begged to retire on old bones to his village fields; he was again summoned and made Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Gui thereupon begged to retire on old bones to his village fields; he was again summoned and made Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 冀暴虐日甚，龜上疏言其罪狀，請誅之，帝不省。

translations.literal: Ji's violence and cruelty grew daily; Gui submitted a memorial stating his crimes and asking that he be executed; the Emperor did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's violence and cruelty grew daily; Gui submitted a memorial stating his crimes and asking that he be executed; the Emperor did not heed it.

sentences.zh: 龜自知必為冀所害，不食七日而死。

translations.literal: Gui knew he would surely be harmed by Ji; he ate nothing for seven days and died.
translations.idiomatic: Gui knew he would surely be harmed by Ji; he ate nothing for seven days and died.

sentences.zh: 種暠到營所，先宣恩信，誘降諸胡，其有不服，然後加討；

translations.literal: When Chong Hao arrived at the camp, he first proclaimed grace and trust, enticed the various Hu to submit; those who would not submit, only then did he add punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong Hao arrived at the camp, he first proclaimed grace and trust and enticed the various Hu to submit; those who would not submit, only then did he add punishment.

sentences.zh: 羌虜先時有生見獲質於郡縣者，悉遣還之；

translations.literal: Qiang and Rong who earlier had living captives held as hostages in the commanderies and counties were all sent back;
translations.idiomatic: Qiang and Rong who earlier had living captives held as hostages in the commanderies and counties were all sent back;

sentences.zh: 誠心懷撫，信賞分明，由是羌、胡皆來順服。

translations.literal: with sincere heart he embraced and comforted them, rewards and punishments clear; thereby the Qiang and Hu all came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: with sincere heart he embraced and comforted them, rewards and punishments clear; thereby the Qiang and Hu all came to submit.

sentences.zh: 暠乃去烽燧，除候望，邊方晏然無警；

translations.literal: Hao then removed beacon fires and abolished watch and lookout; the frontier was tranquil without alarm;
translations.idiomatic: Hao then removed beacon fires and abolished watch and lookout; the frontier was tranquil without alarm;

sentences.zh: 入為大司農。

translations.literal: he entered office as Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，鮮卑寇雁門。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, the Xianbei raided Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, the Xianbei raided Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡夷寇蠶陵。

translations.literal: The Yi of Shu Commandery raided Canling.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi of Shu Commandery raided Canling.

sentences.zh: 三月，復斷刺史、二千石行三年喪。

translations.literal: In the third month, the three-year mourning for inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials was again cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the three-year mourning for inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials was again cut off.

sentences.zh: 夏，京師大水。

translations.literal: In summer, great floods struck the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, great floods struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 六月，鮮卑寇遼東。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Xianbei raided Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the Xianbei raided Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 梁皇后恃姊、兄廕勢，恣極奢靡，兼倍前世，專寵妒忌，六宮莫得進見。

translations.literal: Empress Liang relied on the influence of her elder sister and brothers, indulging to the utmost in luxury, doubling the previous age, monopolizing favor and jealousy; the six palaces could not gain audience.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liang relied on the influence of her elder sister and brothers, indulging to the utmost in luxury, doubling the previous age, monopolizing favor and jealousy; the six palaces could not gain audience.

sentences.zh: 及太后崩，恩寵頓衰。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager died, favor suddenly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager died, favor suddenly declined.

sentences.zh: 後既無嗣，每宮人孕育，鮮得全者。

translations.literal: The empress had no heir; whenever palace women conceived, few infants survived intact.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had no heir; whenever palace women conceived, few infants survived intact.

sentences.zh: 帝雖迫畏梁冀，不敢譴怒，然進御轉希，後益憂恚。

translations.literal: Though the Emperor was compelled and feared Liang Ji and dared not reprove in anger, yet his visits to the inner quarters grew rare and the empress grew ever more sorrowful and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Emperor was compelled and feared Liang Ji and dared not reprove in anger, yet his visits to the inner quarters grew rare and the empress grew ever more sorrowful and resentful.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙午，皇后梁氏崩。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day bingwu, Empress Liang died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on bingwu day, Empress Liang died.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，葬懿獻皇后於懿陵。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, Empress Yixian was buried at Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day, Empress Yixian was buried at Yiling.

sentences.zh: 梁冀一門，前後七侯，三皇后，六貴人，二大將軍，夫人、女食邑稱君者七人，尚公主者三人，其餘卿、將、尹、校五十七人。

translations.literal: The Liang clan, before and after, produced seven marquises, three empresses, six honored ladies, two grand generals; ladies and daughters with fiefs styled lady numbered seven; those who married princesses numbered three; the rest—ministers, generals, chief administrators, and colonels—numbered fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang clan, before and after, produced seven marquises, three empresses, six honored ladies, two grand generals; ladies and daughters with fiefs styled lady numbered seven; those who married princesses numbered three; the rest—ministers, generals, chief administrators, and colonels—numbered fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 冀專擅威柄，凶恣日積，宮衛近侍，並樹所親，禁省起居，纖微必知。

translations.literal: Ji monopolized power and authority; violence and arrogance accumulated daily; palace guards and close attendants all planted his intimates; prohibited quarters and daily life—every trifle he knew.
translations.idiomatic: Ji monopolized power and authority; violence and arrogance accumulated daily; palace guards and close attendants all planted his intimates; prohibited quarters and daily life—every trifle he knew.

sentences.zh: 其四方調發，歲時貢獻，皆先輸上第於冀，乘輿乃其次焉。

translations.literal: Whatever was levied from the four quarters and yearly tribute—all were first delivered in top grade to Ji; the imperial carriage came second.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever was levied from the four quarters and yearly tribute—all were first delivered in top grade to Ji; the imperial carriage came second.

sentences.zh: 吏民繼貨求官、請罪者，道路相望。

translations.literal: Officials and people who succeeded in goods to seek office or plead guilt—on the roads they faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people who succeeded in goods to seek office or plead guilt—on the roads they faced one another.

sentences.zh: 百官遷召，皆先到冀門箋檄謝恩，然後敢詣尚書。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials were promoted and summoned, all first went to Ji's gate with a note of thanks for grace; only then did they dare go to the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the hundred officials were promoted and summoned, all first went to Ji's gate with a note of thanks for grace; only then did they dare go to the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 下邳吳樹為宛令，之官辭冀，冀賓客布在縣界，以情托樹，樹曰：「小人奸蠹，比屋可誅。

translations.literal: Wu Shu of Xiapi was magistrate of Wan; on taking office he bade farewell to Ji; Ji's clients were spread through the county borders; on private grounds he entrusted Shu; Shu said: "Petty men are wicked parasites—house by house they could be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shu of Xiapi was magistrate of Wan; on taking office he bade farewell to Ji; Ji's clients were spread through the county borders; on private grounds he entrusted Shu; Shu said, "Petty men are wicked parasites—house by house they could be executed."

sentences.zh: 明將軍處上將之位，宜崇賢善以補朝闕。

translations.literal: The enlightened general holds the position of supreme commander; he should honor the worthy and good to repair the court's gaps.
translations.idiomatic: The enlightened general holds the position of supreme commander; he should honor the worthy and good to repair the court's gaps.

sentences.zh: 自侍坐以來，未聞稱一長者，而多托非人，誠非敢聞！

translations.literal: Since I took my seat I have not heard you praise one worthy man, yet you often entrust unworthy men—truly I dare not hear it!"
translations.idiomatic: Since I took my seat I have not heard you praise one worthy man, yet you often entrust unworthy men—truly I dare not hear it!"

sentences.zh: 」冀嘿然不悅。

translations.literal: " Ji fell silent, displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji fell silent, displeased.

sentences.zh: 樹到縣，遂誅殺冀客為人害者數十人。

translations.literal: When Shu arrived at the county, he thereupon executed several tens of Ji's clients who had been harming people.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu arrived at the county, he executed several dozen of Ji's clients who had been preying on the people.

sentences.zh: 樹後為荊州刺史，辭冀，冀鴆之，出，死車上。

translations.literal: Later Shu became Inspector of Jing province; on taking leave of Ji, Ji poisoned him—after he departed, he died in his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shu became Inspector of Jing province. When he went to bid Ji farewell, Ji poisoned him; he died in his carriage on the way out.

sentences.zh: 遼東太守侯猛初拜，不謁冀，冀托以它事腰斬之。

translations.literal: When Hou Meng of Liaodong was first appointed administrator, he did not call on Ji; Ji used another matter as pretext and had him cut in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Meng was first appointed Administrator of Liaodong, he did not call on Ji; Ji used another matter as pretext and had him cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 郎中汝南袁著，年十九，詣闕上書曰：「夫四時之運，功成則退，高爵厚寵，鮮不致災。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Zhu of Runan, nineteen years old, went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, saying: "The cycle of the four seasons—when merit is complete one should withdraw; lofty rank and thick favor rarely fail to bring disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Zhu of Runan, nineteen years old, went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, saying, "The cycle of the four seasons—when merit is complete one should withdraw; lofty rank and thick favor rarely fail to bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 今大將軍位極功成，可為至戒，宜遵縣車之禮，高枕頤神。

translations.literal: Now the Grand General's position is at the utmost and his merit complete—it should be the greatest warning; he should follow the rite of hanging up the carriage, rest his head on a high pillow, and nourish his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Grand General's position is at the utmost and his merit complete—it should be the greatest warning; he should follow the rite of hanging up the carriage, rest his head on a high pillow, and nourish his spirit.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：『木實繁者披枝害心。

translations.literal: The tradition says: 'When a tree's fruit is abundant, its branches are stripped and its heart harmed.
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says, 'When a tree's fruit is abundant, its branches are stripped and its heart harmed.

sentences.zh: 』若不抑損盛權，將無以全其身矣！

translations.literal: ' If one does not restrain and reduce overflowing power, one will have no means to preserve one's person!"
translations.idiomatic: ' If one does not restrain and reduce overflowing power, one will have no means to preserve one's person!"

sentences.zh: 」冀聞而密遣掩捕，著乃變易姓名，托病偽死，結蒲為人，市棺殯送。

translations.literal: " When Ji heard of it he secretly sent men to seize Zhu in a surprise arrest; Zhu then changed his name, feigned illness and sham death, bound rushes into a human form, bought a coffin, and had a funeral procession sent off.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ji heard of it he secretly sent men to seize Zhu in a surprise arrest; Zhu then changed his name, feigned illness and sham death, bound rushes into a human form, bought a coffin, and had a funeral procession sent off.

sentences.zh: 冀知其詐，求得，笞殺之。

translations.literal: Ji knew it was a fraud, found him, and had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Ji knew it was a fraud, found him, and had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 太原郝絜、胡武，好危言高論，與著友善，絜、武嘗連名奏記三府，薦海內高士，而不詣冀。

translations.literal: Hao Jie and Hu Wu of Taiyuan loved bold words and lofty discourse and were friendly with Zhu; Jie and Wu once jointly submitted a note to the three offices recommending eminent men within the seas, yet did not call on Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Jie and Hu Wu of Taiyuan loved bold words and lofty discourse and were friendly with Zhu; Jie and Wu once jointly submitted a note to the three offices recommending eminent men within the seas, yet did not call on Ji.

sentences.zh: 冀追怒之，敕中都官稱檄禽捕，遂誅下家，死者六十餘人。

translations.literal: Ji pursued them in anger, ordered the central palace officials to issue warrants for their arrest, and thereupon executed their households; more than sixty died.
translations.idiomatic: Ji pursued them in anger, ordered the central palace officials to issue warrants for their arrest, and thereupon executed their households; more than sixty died.

sentences.zh: 絜初逃亡，知不得免，因輿梓奏書冀門，書入，仰藥而死，家乃得全。

translations.literal: Jie at first fled; knowing he could not escape, he had a coffin carried and submitted a memorial at Ji's gate; when the memorial was delivered he took poison and died, and his family was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: Jie at first fled; knowing he could not escape, he had a coffin carried and submitted a memorial at Ji's gate; when the memorial was delivered he took poison and died, and his family was thereby spared.

sentences.zh: 安帝嫡母耿貴人薨，冀從貴人從子林慮侯承求貴人珍玩，不能得，冀怒，並族其家十餘人。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Geng, the Emperor's father's principal consort, died, Ji had the honored lady's nephew, Marquis Cheng of Linlu, seek the lady's precious curios; when he could not obtain them Ji grew angry and executed Cheng's entire clan of more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Geng, the Emperor's father's principal consort, died, Ji had the honored lady's nephew, Marquis Cheng of Linlu, seek the lady's precious curios; when he could not obtain them Ji grew angry and executed Cheng's entire clan of more than ten.

sentences.zh: 涿郡崔琦以文章為冀所善，琦作《外戚箴》、《白鵠賦》以風，冀怒。

translations.literal: Cui Qi of Zhuo Commandery was favored by Ji for his literary skill; Qi composed "Admonition on Consort Kin" and "Rhapsody on the White Swan" to admonish him, and Ji grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qi of Zhuo Commandery was favored by Ji for his literary skill; Qi composed "Admonition on Consort Kin" and "Rhapsody on the White Swan" to admonish him, and Ji grew angry.

sentences.zh: 琦曰：「昔管仲相齊，樂聞譏諫之言；

translations.literal: Qi said: "In former times Guan Zhong served as chancellor of Qi and delighted to hear words of criticism and remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "In former times Guan Zhong served as chancellor of Qi and delighted to hear words of criticism and remonstrance;

sentences.zh: 蕭何佐漢，乃設書過之吏。

translations.literal: Xiao He assisted Han and therefore established officials who recorded faults.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He assisted Han and therefore established officials who recorded faults.

sentences.zh: 今將軍屢世台輔，任齊伊、周，而德政未聞，黎元塗炭，不能結納貞良以救禍敗，反欲鉗塞士口，杜蔽主聽，將使玄黃改色、馬鹿易形乎！

translations.literal: Now the General for generations has held the highest ministerial posts, his commission equal to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, yet no virtuous governance is heard; the common people are in utter misery—you cannot gather and win over the upright and good to rescue disaster and ruin, yet instead wish to clamp shut the mouths of scholars and block and blind the ruler's hearing—will you make black turn yellow and deer become horses!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the General for generations has held the highest ministerial posts, his commission equal to Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, yet no virtuous governance is heard; the common people are in utter misery—you cannot gather and win over the upright and good to rescue disaster and ruin, yet instead wish to clamp shut the mouths of scholars and block and blind the ruler's hearing—will you make black turn yellow and deer become horses!"

sentences.zh: 」冀無以對，因遣琦歸。

translations.literal: " Ji had nothing with which to reply and therefore sent Qi home.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji had nothing with which to reply and therefore sent Qi home.

sentences.zh: 琦懼而亡匿，冀捕得，殺之。

translations.literal: Qi, in fear, fled and hid; Ji captured him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, in fear, fled and hid; Ji captured him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 冀秉政幾二十年，威行內外，天子拱手，不得有所親與，帝既不平之；

translations.literal: Ji held power for nearly twenty years; his authority extended inside and outside; the Son of Heaven stood with folded hands and could not personally attend to affairs—the Emperor was already displeased;
translations.idiomatic: Ji held power for nearly twenty years; his authority extended inside and outside; the Son of Heaven stood with folded hands and could not personally attend to affairs—the Emperor was already displeased;

sentences.zh: 及陳授死，帝愈怒。

translations.literal: when Chen Shou died the Emperor grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: when Chen Shou died the Emperor grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 和熹皇后從兄子郎中鄧香妻宣，生女猛，香卒，宣更適梁紀；

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Deng Xiang, a son of Empress Dowager Hexi's cousin, had a wife named Xuan who bore a daughter Meng; when Xiang died, Xuan remarried Liang Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary Deng Xiang, a son of Empress Dowager Hexi's cousin, had a wife named Xuan who bore a daughter Meng; when Xiang died, Xuan remarried Liang Ji;

sentences.zh: 紀，孫壽之舅也。

translations.literal: Ji was the maternal uncle of Sun Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was the maternal uncle of Sun Shou.

sentences.zh: 壽以猛色美，引入掖庭，為貴人，冀欲認猛為其女，易猛姓為梁。

translations.literal: Shou, because Meng's beauty was fine, brought her into the rear palace as an honored lady; Ji wished to claim Meng as his daughter and changed Meng's surname to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Shou, because Meng's beauty was fine, brought her into the rear palace as an honored lady; Ji wished to claim Meng as his daughter and changed Meng's surname to Liang.

sentences.zh: 冀恐猛姊婿議郎邴尊沮敗宣意，遣客刺殺之。

translations.literal: Ji feared that Meng's elder sister's husband, Consultant Bing Zun, would thwart and ruin Xuan's intent, and sent a client to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji feared that Meng's elder sister's husband, Consultant Bing Zun, would thwart and ruin Xuan's intent, and sent a client to assassinate him.

sentences.zh: 又欲殺宣，宣家與中常侍袁赦相比，冀客登赦屋，欲入宣家，赦覺之，鳴鼓會眾以告宣。

translations.literal: He also wished to kill Xuan; Xuan's household adjoined that of Regular Palace Attendant Yuan She; Ji's client climbed onto She's roof intending to enter Xuan's house; She noticed it, beat the drum and gathered the crowd to inform Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to kill Xuan; Xuan's household adjoined that of Regular Palace Attendant Yuan She; Ji's client climbed onto She's roof intending to enter Xuan's house; She noticed it, beat the drum and gathered the crowd to inform Xuan.

sentences.zh: 宣馳入白帝，帝大怒，因如廁，獨呼小黃門史唐衡，問：「左右與外捨不相得者，誰乎？

translations.literal: Xuan rushed in to inform the Emperor; the Emperor was greatly angered; then, as if going to the privy, he alone summoned Junior Yellow Gate Attendant Tang Heng and asked: "Among those close at hand and the outer household, who are not on good terms?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan rushed in to inform the Emperor; the Emperor was greatly angered; then, as if going to the privy, he alone summoned Junior Yellow Gate Attendant Tang Heng and asked, "Among those close at hand and the outer household, who are not on good terms?"

sentences.zh: 」衡對：「中常侍單超、小黃門史左心官與梁不疑有隙；

translations.literal: " Heng replied: "Regular Palace Attendant Shan Chao and Junior Yellow Gate Attendant Zuo Xinguan have a rift with Liang Buyi;
translations.idiomatic: " Heng replied, "Regular Palace Attendant Shan Chao and Junior Yellow Gate Attendant Zuo Xinguan have a rift with Liang Buyi;

sentences.zh: 中常侍徐璜、黃門令具瑗常私忿疾外捨放橫，口不敢道。

translations.literal: Regular Palace Attendant Xu Huang and Yellow Gate Commandant Ju Yuan often privately resent the outer household's arrogance and violence, yet dare not speak of it in their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Palace Attendant Xu Huang and Yellow Gate Commandant Ju Yuan often privately resent the outer household's arrogance and violence, yet dare not speak of it in their mouths.

sentences.zh: 」於是帝呼超、心官入室，謂曰：「梁將軍兄弟專朝，迫脅內外，公卿以下，從其風旨，今欲誅之，於常侍意如何？

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Emperor summoned Chao and Xinguan into the room and said: "General Liang and his brothers monopolize the court, coercing inside and outside; ministers and officials below follow their intent—now I wish to execute them; what do the regular attendants think?"
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the Emperor summoned Chao and Xinguan into the room and said, "General Liang and his brothers monopolize the court, coercing inside and outside; ministers and officials below follow their intent—now I wish to execute them; what do the regular attendants think?"

sentences.zh: 」超等對曰：「誠國奸賊，當誅日久；

translations.literal: " Chao and the others replied: "They are truly traitors of the state and should long ago have been executed;
translations.idiomatic: " Chao and the others replied, "They are truly traitors of the state and should long ago have been executed;

sentences.zh: 臣等弱劣，未知聖意如何耳。

translations.literal: we your servants are weak and inferior and do not know what Your Sage intent may be."
translations.idiomatic: we your servants are weak and inferior and do not know what Your Sage intent may be."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「審然者，常侍密圖之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "If it is truly so, let the regular attendants secretly plan it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "If it is truly so, let the regular attendants secretly plan it.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「圖之不難，但恐陛下腹中狐疑。

translations.literal: " They replied: "Planning it is not difficult, but we fear doubt lingering in Your Majesty's belly.
translations.idiomatic: " They replied, "Planning it is not difficult, but we fear doubt lingering in Your Majesty's belly.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「奸臣脅國，當伏其罪，何疑乎！

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Traitorous ministers coerce the state—they should suffer their punishment; what doubt is there!"
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "Traitorous ministers coerce the state—they should suffer their punishment; what doubt is there!"

sentences.zh: 」於是更召璜、瑗等，五人共定其議，帝齧超臂出血為盟。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he further summoned Huang, Yuan, and the others; the five men together fixed the plan, and the Emperor bit Chao's arm until blood flowed as their covenant.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he further summoned Huang, Yuan, and the others; the five men together fixed the plan, and the Emperor bit Chao's arm until blood flowed as their covenant.

sentences.zh: 超等曰：「陛下今計已決，勿復更言，恐為人所疑。

translations.literal: Chao and the others said: "Your Majesty's plan is now decided—do not speak of it again, lest others become suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Chao and the others said, "Your Majesty's plan is now decided—do not speak of it again, lest others become suspicious.

sentences.zh: 冀心疑超等，八月，丁丑，使中黃門張惲入省宿，以防其變。

translations.literal: Ji suspected Chao and the others; in the eighth month, on the day dingchou, he sent Central Yellow Gate Attendant Zhang Yun to lodge inside the palace precinct to guard against any upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: Ji suspected Chao and the others; in the eighth month, on dingchou day, he sent Central Yellow Gate Attendant Zhang Yun to lodge inside the palace precinct to guard against any upheaval.

sentences.zh: 具瑗敕吏收惲，以「輒從外入，欲圖不軌。

translations.literal: Ju Yuan ordered officials to arrest Yun on the charge that "he rashly entered from outside intending to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Yuan ordered officials to arrest Yun on the charge that "he rashly entered from outside intending to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」帝御前殿，召諸尚書入，發其事，使尚書令尹勳持節勒丞、郎以下皆操兵守省閣，斂諸符節送省中，使具瑗將左右廄騶、虎賁、羽林、都候劍戟士合千餘人，與司隸校尉張彪共圍冀第，使光祿勳袁□於持節收冀大將軍印綬，徙封比景都鄉侯。

translations.literal: " The Emperor took the front hall, summoned all the Masters of Writing in, disclosed the affair, and had Master of Writing Yin Xun hold the staff of authority to command assistants, attendants, and below all to take up arms and guard the provincial offices; all tally-seals were gathered and sent into the palace precinct; Ju Yuan was made to lead more than a thousand sword-and-halberd men of the left and right stables, tiger guards, feathered forest, and capital guards, and together with Colonel of the Region Zhang Biao surround Ji's mansion; he had Household Minister Yuan Fuzi hold the staff of authority to receive Ji's Grand General seal and cord and demote him to Marquis of Bijing Capital Village.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor took the front hall, summoned all the Masters of Writing in, disclosed the affair, and had Master of Writing Yin Xun hold the staff of authority to command assistants, attendants, and below all to take up arms and guard the provincial offices; all tally-seals were gathered and sent into the palace precinct; Ju Yuan was made to lead more than a thousand sword-and-halberd men of the left and right stables, tiger guards, feathered forest, and capital guards, and together with Colonel of the Region Zhang Biao surround Ji's mansion; he had Household Minister Yuan Fuzi hold the staff of authority to receive Ji's Grand General seal and cord and demote him to Marquis of Bijing Capital Village.

sentences.zh: 冀及妻壽即日皆自殺；

translations.literal: Ji and his wife Shou that same day both killed themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Ji and his wife Shou that same day both killed themselves;

sentences.zh: 不疑、蒙先卒。

translations.literal: Buyi and Meng had already died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Buyi and Meng had already died earlier.

sentences.zh: 悉收梁氏、孫氏中外宗親送詔獄，無長少皆棄市；

translations.literal: All the Liang and Sun clans' kin inside and outside were seized and sent to the imperial prison; none, old or young, escaped execution in the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: All the Liang and Sun clans' kin inside and outside were seized and sent to the imperial prison; none, old or young, escaped execution in the marketplace;

sentences.zh: 它所連及公卿、列校、刺史、二千石，死者數十人。

translations.literal: those elsewhere implicated—ministers, colonels, inspectors, and two-thousand-bushel officials—numbered several tens dead.
translations.idiomatic: those elsewhere implicated—ministers, colonels, inspectors, and two-thousand-bushel officials—numbered several tens dead.

sentences.zh: 太尉胡廣、司徒韓縯、司空孫朗皆坐阿附梁冀，不衛宮，止長壽亭，減死一等，免為庶人。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Hu Guang, Minister over the Masses Han Yan, and Minister of Works Sun Lang were all charged with fawning on and attaching themselves to Liang Ji, failing to guard the palace, and stopping at Changshou Pavilion; their death sentences were reduced one degree and they were dismissed as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Hu Guang, Minister over the Masses Han Yan, and Minister of Works Sun Lang were all charged with fawning on and attaching themselves to Liang Ji, failing to guard the palace, and stopping at Changshou Pavilion; their death sentences were reduced one degree and they were dismissed as commoners.

sentences.zh: 故吏、賓客免黜者三百餘人，朝廷為空。

translations.literal: Former clerks and clients dismissed numbered more than three hundred; the court was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Former clerks and clients dismissed numbered more than three hundred; the court was emptied.

sentences.zh: 是時，事猝從中發，使者交馳，公卿失其度，官府市裡鼎沸，數日乃定；

translations.literal: At this time the affair suddenly erupted from within; messengers crossed paths in haste; ministers and officials lost their composure; government offices and market streets seethed like a boiling cauldron—only after several days did it settle;
translations.idiomatic: At this time the affair suddenly erupted from within; messengers crossed paths in haste; ministers and officials lost their composure; government offices and market streets seethed like a boiling cauldron—only after several days did it settle;

sentences.zh: 百姓莫不稱慶。

translations.literal: the common people all voiced celebration.
translations.idiomatic: the common people all voiced celebration.

sentences.zh: 收冀財貨，縣官斥賣，合三十餘萬萬，以充王府用，減天下稅租之半，散其苑囿，以業窮民。

translations.literal: Ji's goods and wealth were seized and sold off by the government; the total reached more than three hundred million; it was used to fill the imperial treasury, half the empire's taxes and land rents were reduced, and his parks and preserves were opened to give livelihood to the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's goods and wealth were seized and sold off by the government; the total reached more than three hundred million; it was used to fill the imperial treasury, half the empire's taxes and land rents were reduced, and his parks and preserves were opened to give livelihood to the destitute.

sentences.zh: 壬午，立梁貴人為皇后，追廢懿陵為貴人塚。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Honored Lady Liang was established as empress; Yiling was retroactively demoted to an honored lady's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day, Honored Lady Liang was established as empress; Yiling was retroactively demoted to an honored lady's tomb.

sentences.zh: 帝惡梁氏，改皇后姓為薄氏，久之，知為鄧香女，乃複姓鄧氏。

translations.literal: The Emperor hated the Liang clan and changed the empress's surname to Bo; after a long time, learning she was Deng Xiang's daughter, he restored the surname Deng.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hated the Liang clan and changed the empress's surname to Bo; after a long time, learning she was Deng Xiang's daughter, he restored the surname Deng.

sentences.zh: 詔賞誅梁冀之功，封單超、徐璜、具瑗、左心官、唐衡皆為縣侯，超食二萬戶，璜等各萬餘戶，世謂之五侯。

translations.literal: An edict rewarded the merit of executing Liang Ji; Shan Chao, Xu Huang, Ju Yuan, Zuo Xinguan, and Tang Heng were all enfeoffed as district marquises; Chao's fief was twenty thousand households, Huang and the others each more than ten thousand households—the age called them the Five Marquises.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rewarded the merit of executing Liang Ji; Shan Chao, Xu Huang, Ju Yuan, Zuo Xinguan, and Tang Heng were all enfeoffed as district marquises; Chao's fief was twenty thousand households, Huang and the others each more than ten thousand households—the age called them the Five Marquises.

sentences.zh: 仍以心官、衡為中常侍。

translations.literal: Xinguan and Heng were further made regular palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Xinguan and Heng were further made regular palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 又封尚書令尹勳等七人皆為亭侯。

translations.literal: Seven men including Master of Writing Yin Xun were also enfeoffed as village marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Seven men including Master of Writing Yin Xun were also enfeoffed as village marquises.

sentences.zh: 以大司農黃瓊為太尉，光祿大夫中山祝恬為司徒，大鴻臚梁國盛允為司空。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture Huang Qiong was made Grand Commandant; Household Grandee Zhu Ti of Zhongshan was made Minister over the Masses; Grand Herald Sheng Yun of Liang was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Agriculture Huang Qiong was made Grand Commandant; Household Grandee Zhu Ti of Zhongshan was made Minister over the Masses; Grand Herald Sheng Yun of Liang was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 是時，新誅梁冀，天下想望異政，黃瓊首居公位，乃舉奏州郡素行貪污，至死徙者十餘人，海內翕然稱之。

translations.literal: At this time, with Liang Ji newly executed, all under heaven looked for a different governance; Huang Qiong, first among the highest offices, thereupon memorialized and impeached those in the provinces and commanderies whose conduct had long been corrupt—more than ten suffered death or banishment—and within the seas praise arose as one.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, with Liang Ji newly executed, all under heaven looked for a different governance; Huang Qiong, first among the highest offices, thereupon memorialized and impeached those in the provinces and commanderies whose conduct had long been corrupt—more than ten suffered death or banishment—and within the seas praise arose as one.

sentences.zh: 瓊辟汝南范滂。

translations.literal: Qiong recruited Fan Pang of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong recruited Fan Pang of Runan.

sentences.zh: 滂少厲清節，為州裡所服。

translations.literal: Pang from youth cultivated pure integrity and was respected by his province and village.
translations.idiomatic: Pang from youth cultivated pure integrity and was respected by his province and village.

sentences.zh: 嘗為清詔使，案察冀州，滂登車攬轡，慨然有澄清天下之志。

translations.literal: He once served as Purifying Edict Emissary, investigating Ji province; Pang mounted his carriage and took the reins, sighing with the ambition to clarify all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as Purifying Edict Emissary, investigating Ji province; Pang mounted his carriage and took the reins, sighing with the ambition to clarify all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 守令臧污者，皆望風解印綬去；

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates who were corrupt all, at the sight of his approach, surrendered their seals and cords and departed;
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt prefects and magistrates all surrendered their seals and cords and fled at his approach;

sentences.zh: 其所舉奏，莫不厭塞眾議。

translations.literal: those he memorialized and impeached all silenced the crowd's objections.
translations.idiomatic: those he memorialized and impeached all silenced the crowd's objections.

sentences.zh: 會詔三府掾屬舉謠言，滂奏刺史、二千石權豪之黨二十餘人。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered the three offices' staff to report slanderous speech, Pang memorialized more than twenty partisans of inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials among the powerful and great.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the three offices' staff to report slanderous speech, Pang memorialized more than twenty partisans of inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials among the powerful and great.

sentences.zh: 尚書責滂所劾猥多，疑有私故。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing reproached Pang for impeaching too many and suspected private motives.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing reproached Pang for impeaching too many and suspected private motives.

sentences.zh: 滂對曰：「臣之所舉，自非叨穢奸暴，深為民害，豈以污簡札哉！

translations.literal: Pang replied: "Those your servant has impeached—unless they were greedy, filthy, wicked, and violent, deeply harming the people—how could I stain the bamboo slips!"
translations.idiomatic: Pang replied, "Those your servant has impeached—unless they were greedy, filthy, wicked, and violent, deeply harming the people—how could I stain the bamboo slips!"

sentences.zh: 間以會日迫促，故先舉所急，其未審者，方更參實。

translations.literal: Only because the assembly day was pressing I first impeached what was urgent; what is not yet verified I shall further investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Only because the assembly day was pressing I first impeached what was urgent; what is not yet verified I shall further investigate.

sentences.zh: 臣聞農夫去草，嘉谷必茂；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when a farmer removes weeds, fine grain must flourish;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that when a farmer removes weeds, fine grain must flourish;

sentences.zh: 忠臣除奸，王道以清。

translations.literal: when a loyal minister removes the wicked, the kingly way is thereby clarified.
translations.idiomatic: when a loyal minister removes the wicked, the kingly way is thereby clarified.

sentences.zh: 若臣言有貳，甘受顯戮！

translations.literal: If your servant's words are false, I willingly accept open execution!"
translations.idiomatic: If your servant's words are false, I willingly accept open execution!"

sentences.zh: 」尚書不能詰。

translations.literal: " The Masters of Writing could not cross-examine him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Masters of Writing could not cross-examine him.

sentences.zh: 尚書令陳蕃上疏薦五處士，豫章徐稚、彭城姜肱、汝南袁閎、京兆韋著，穎川李曇。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Chen Fan submitted a memorial recommending five recluses: Xu Zhi of Yuzhang, Jiang Gong of Pengcheng, Yuan Hong of Runan, Wei Zhu of Jingzhao, and Li Tan of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Chen Fan submitted a memorial recommending five recluses: Xu Zhi of Yuzhang, Jiang Gong of Pengcheng, Yuan Hong of Runan, Wei Zhu of Jingzhao, and Li Tan of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 帝悉以安車、玄纁備禮征之，皆不至。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent for them all with a comfortable carriage, dark scarlet robes, and full ceremony—they none came.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent for them all with a comfortable carriage, dark scarlet robes, and full ceremony—they none came.

sentences.zh: 稚家貧，常自耕稼，非其力不食，恭儉義讓，所居服其德；

translations.literal: Zhi's family was poor; he often tilled the fields himself, eating nothing not earned by his own labor; respectful, frugal, righteous, and yielding—where he lived people submitted to his virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's family was poor; he often tilled the fields himself, eating nothing not earned by his own labor; respectful, frugal, righteous, and yielding—where he lived people submitted to his virtue;

sentences.zh: 屢辟公府，不起。

translations.literal: repeatedly summoned by the highest offices, he would not rise to serve.
translations.idiomatic: repeatedly summoned by the highest offices, he would not rise to serve.

sentences.zh: 陳蕃為豫章太守，以禮請署功曹；

translations.literal: When Chen Fan was Administrator of Yuzhang, he courteously invited Zhi to take the post of Merit Officer;
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Fan was Administrator of Yuzhang, he courteously invited Zhi to take the post of Merit Officer;

sentences.zh: 稚不之免，既謁而退。

translations.literal: Zhi did not exempt himself from the visit; after paying his respects he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi did not exempt himself from the visit; after paying his respects he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蕃性方峻，不接賓客，唯稚來，特設一榻，去則縣之。

translations.literal: Fan's nature was upright and stern; he did not receive guests—only when Zhi came did he specially set out one couch, and when Zhi left he hung it up.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's nature was upright and stern; he did not receive guests—only when Zhi came did he specially set out one couch, and when Zhi left he hung it up.

sentences.zh: 後舉有道，家拜太原太守，皆不就。

translations.literal: Later he was recommended as a man of the Way and was appointed by imperial letter as Administrator of Taiyuan—he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recommended as a man of the Way and was appointed by imperial letter as Administrator of Taiyuan—he accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 稚雖不應諸公之辟，然聞其死喪，輒負笈赴吊。

translations.literal: Though Zhi did not respond to the summons of the great lords, whenever he heard of a death or mourning he would shoulder his book-chest and hurry to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhi did not respond to the summons of the great lords, whenever he heard of a death or mourning he would shoulder his book-chest and hurry to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 常於家豫炙雞一隻，以一兩綿絮漬酒中暴干，以裹雞，逕到所赴塚隧外，以水漬綿，使有酒氣，斗米飯，白茅為藉。

translations.literal: He would often at home beforehand roast one chicken, soak an ounce or two of cotton wadding in wine and sun-dry it, wrap the chicken with it, go straight to outside the tomb passage he was visiting, soak the cotton with water until it gave off a wine scent, set out a peck of rice, and spread white thatch as a mat.
translations.idiomatic: He would often at home beforehand roast one chicken, soak an ounce or two of cotton wadding in wine and sun-dry it, wrap the chicken with it, go straight to outside the tomb passage he was visiting, soak the cotton with water until it gave off a wine scent, set out a peck of rice, and spread white thatch as a mat.

sentences.zh: 以雞置前，醊酒畢，留謁則去，不見喪主。

translations.literal: He placed the chicken before the tomb, finished the libation wine, left his name card of visit, and departed—he did not meet the bereaved host.
translations.idiomatic: He placed the chicken before the tomb, finished the libation wine, left his name card of visit, and departed—he did not meet the bereaved host.

sentences.zh: 肱與二弟仲海、季江俱以孝友著聞，常同被而寢，不應徵聘。

translations.literal: Gong and his two younger brothers Zhonghai and Jijiang were all famed for filial piety and brotherly affection; they often shared one cover while sleeping and did not respond to summons and appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Gong and his two younger brothers Zhonghai and Jijiang were all famed for filial piety and brotherly affection; they often shared one cover while sleeping and did not respond to summons and appointments.

sentences.zh: 肱嘗與弟季江俱詣郡，夜於道為盜所劫，欲殺之，肱曰：「弟年幼，父母所憐，又未聘娶，願殺身濟弟。

translations.literal: Gong once went with his brother Jijiang together to the commandery seat; at night on the road they were robbed by bandits who wished to kill them; Gong said: "My brother is young, beloved of our parents, and not yet betrothed—I wish to give my life to save my brother.
translations.idiomatic: Gong once went with his brother Jijiang together to the commandery seat; at night on the road they were robbed by bandits who wished to kill them; Gong said, "My brother is young, beloved of our parents, and not yet betrothed—I wish to give my life to save my brother.

sentences.zh: 」季江曰：「兄年德在前，家之珍寶，國之英俊，乞自受戮，以代兄命。

translations.literal: " Jijiang said: "Elder brother, your years and virtue come first—you are the family's treasure and the state's fine talent; I beg to accept execution myself in place of my elder brother's life.
translations.idiomatic: " Jijiang said, "Elder brother, your years and virtue come first—you are the family's treasure and the state's fine talent; I beg to accept execution myself in place of my elder brother's life.

sentences.zh: 」盜遂兩釋焉，但掠奪衣資而已。

translations.literal: " The bandits thereupon released them both, plundering only clothes and goods.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandits thereupon released them both, plundering only clothes and goods.

sentences.zh: 既至，郡中見肱無衣服，怪問其故，肱托以它辭，終不言盜。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the commandery saw Gong without clothes and asked in wonder the reason; Gong put it off with other words and to the end did not speak of the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, the commandery saw Gong without clothes and asked in wonder the reason; Gong put it off with other words and to the end did not speak of the bandits.

sentences.zh: 盜聞而感悔，就精廬求見征君，叩頭謝罪，還所略物。

translations.literal: The bandits, hearing of it, were moved to repentance; they went to the hermitage seeking to see the recluse lord, kowtowed in apology, and returned what they had plundered.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, hearing of it, were moved to repentance; they went to the hermitage seeking to see the recluse lord, kowtowed in apology, and returned what they had plundered.

sentences.zh: 肱不受，勞以酒食而遣之。

translations.literal: Gong did not accept them, but treated them with wine and food and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Gong did not accept them, but treated them with wine and food and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 帝既征肱不至，乃下彭城，使畫工圖其形狀。

translations.literal: Since the Emperor had summoned Gong and he had not come, he went down to Pengcheng and had painters depict his likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Emperor had summoned Gong and he had not come, he went down to Pengcheng and had painters depict his likeness.

sentences.zh: 肱臥於幽暗，以被韜面，言患眩疾，不欲出風，工竟不得見之。

translations.literal: Gong lay in a dark place, covered his face with the quilt, and said he suffered dizzy sickness and did not wish to meet the wind—the painters in the end could not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Gong lay in a dark place, covered his face with the quilt, and said he suffered dizzy sickness and did not wish to meet the wind—the painters in the end could not see him.

sentences.zh: 閎，安之玄孫也，苦身修節，不應辟召。

translations.literal: Hong was the great-great-grandson of Yuan An; he mortified the body and cultivated integrity and did not respond to summons.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was the great-great-grandson of Yuan An; he mortified the body and cultivated integrity and did not respond to summons.

sentences.zh: 著隱居講授，不修世務。

translations.literal: Zhu lived in seclusion lecturing and did not attend to worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu lived in seclusion lecturing and did not attend to worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 曇繼母酷烈，曇奉之逾謹，得四時珍玩，未嘗不先拜而後進，鄉里以為法。

translations.literal: Tan had a stepmother fierce and harsh; Tan served her with ever greater care—whenever he obtained seasonal delicacies and curios he never failed first to bow and only then present them; the village took this as a model.
translations.idiomatic: Tan had a stepmother fierce and harsh; Tan served her with ever greater care—whenever he obtained seasonal delicacies and curios he never failed first to bow and only then present them; the village took this as a model.

sentences.zh: 帝又征安陽魏桓，其鄉人勸之行，桓曰：「夫干祿求進，所以行其志也。

translations.literal: The Emperor again summoned Wei Huan of Anyang; his fellow villagers urged him to go; Huan said: "Seeking salary and advancement is the means by which one carries out one's will.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again summoned Wei Huan of Anyang; his fellow villagers urged him to go; Huan said, "Seeking salary and advancement is the means by which one carries out one's will.

sentences.zh: 今後宮千數，其可損乎？

translations.literal: Now the rear palace numbers in the thousands—can that be reduced?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the rear palace numbers in the thousands—can that be reduced?"

sentences.zh: 廄馬萬匹，其可減乎？

translations.literal: Stable horses number ten thousand—can that be reduced?"
translations.idiomatic: Stable horses number ten thousand—can that be reduced?"

sentences.zh: 左右權豪，其可去乎？

translations.literal: Powerful great ones at hand—can they be removed?"
translations.idiomatic: Powerful great ones at hand—can they be removed?"

sentences.zh: 」皆對曰：「不可。

translations.literal: " All replied: "It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: " All replied, "It cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 」桓乃慨然歎曰：「使桓生行死歸，於諸子何有哉！

translations.literal: " Huan then sighed with feeling and said: "If Huan is born walking and dies returning—what has that to do with the rest of you!"
translations.idiomatic: " Huan then sighed with feeling and said, "If Huan is born walking and dies returning—what has that to do with the rest of you!"

sentences.zh: 」遂隱身不出。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon he hid himself and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he went into hiding and never emerged.

sentences.zh: 帝既誅梁冀，故舊恩敵，多受封爵：追贈皇后父鄧香為車騎將軍，封安陽侯；

translations.literal: The Emperor, having already executed Liang Ji, saw many old friends, favored ones, and enemies alike receive enfeoffments and ranks: posthumously enfeoffing the Empress's father Deng Xiang as General of Chariots and Cavalry and as Marquis of Anyang;
translations.idiomatic: Once Liang Ji was dead, the Emperor lavished titles on old friends, favorites, and former foes alike: the Empress's father Deng Xiang was posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anyang;

sentences.zh: 更封後母宣為昆陽君，兄子康、秉皆為列侯，宗族皆列校、郎將，賞賜以巨萬計。

translations.literal: Further enfeoffing the stepmother Xuan as Lady of Kunyang; nephew Kang and Bing both as full marquises; the clan all as colonels and gentleman-generals; rewards and gifts reckoned in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He further enfeoffed his stepmother Xuan as Lady of Kunyang, made his nephews Kang and Bing full marquises, appointed the whole clan as colonels and gentleman-generals, and showered rewards counted in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 中常侍侯覽上縑五千匹，帝賜爵關內侯，又托以與議誅冀，進封高鄉侯；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Hou Lan presented five thousand bolts of silk; the Emperor granted him rank as Marquis Within the Passes, and further, on the pretext of having joined in plotting Liang Ji's execution, advanced him to Marquis of Gaoxiang;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Hou Lan offered five thousand bolts of silk. The Emperor made him Marquis Within the Passes and, citing his role in plotting Liang Ji's downfall, promoted him to Marquis of Gaoxiang;

sentences.zh: 又封小黃門劉普、趙忠等八人為鄉侯。

translations.literal: He also enfeoffed eight men including Junior Palace Attendants Liu Pu and Zhao Zhong as township marquises.
translations.idiomatic: He also enfeoffed eight men, including Junior Palace Attendants Liu Pu and Zhao Zhong, as township marquises.

sentences.zh: 自是權勢專歸宦官矣。

translations.literal: From this time power and influence belonged exclusively to the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, power passed entirely into eunuch hands.

sentences.zh: 五侯尤貪縱，傾動內外。

translations.literal: The Five Marquises were especially greedy and unrestrained, shaking inner and outer courts alike.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Marquises were greedier and more unrestrained than any, and their sway rocked court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 時災異數見，白馬令甘陵李雲露布上書，移副三府曰：「梁冀雖持權專擅，虐流天下，今以罪行誅，猶召家臣扼殺之耳，而猥封謀臣萬戶以上；

translations.literal: At this time portents and anomalies appeared repeatedly. Li Yun of Ganling, magistrate of Baima, posted an open letter memorial and sent copies to the Three Excellencies, saying: "Though Liang Ji wielded power despotically and his cruelty spread through the realm, he was now executed for his crimes—yet that was no more than summoning a household retainer to strangle him—and yet you rashly enfeoff the plotters with ten-thousand-household marquisates and above;
translations.idiomatic: Portents multiplied. Li Yun of Ganling, magistrate of Baima, posted an open memorial and copied it to the Three Excellencies: "Liang Ji tyrannized the realm, yet his execution was no more than having a household servant throttle him—and now the conspirators are rashly enfeoffed as ten-thousand-household marquises and above;

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，得無見非！

translations.literal: If Emperor Gaozu heard of this, would he not find fault!
translations.idiomatic: Would Emperor Gaozu not take offense at this!

sentences.zh: 西北列將，得無解體！

translations.literal: Would the frontier generals of the northwest not lose heart!
translations.idiomatic: Would the frontier generals of the northwest not fall apart in despair!

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『帝者，諦也。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'The emperor—di—is one who examines closely.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: 'The emperor—di—is one who listens closely.

sentences.zh: 』今官位錯亂，小人諂進，財貨公行，政化日損；

translations.literal: 』Today offices and ranks are in disorder, petty men advance through flattery, wealth and goods are traded openly, and governance daily declines;
translations.idiomatic: 』Today ranks are scrambled, flatterers rise, bribes pass openly, and governance erodes day by day;

sentences.zh: 尺一拜用，不經御省，是帝欲不謗乎！

translations.literal: Imperial appointments issued on foot-long slips are put into use without passing imperial review—is this an emperor who does not wish to be criticized!
translations.idiomatic: Imperial appointments on foot-long slips take effect without the Emperor's review—is this an emperor who does not wish to hear criticism!

sentences.zh: 」帝得奏震怒，下有司逮雲，詔尚書都護劍戟送黃門北寺獄，使中常侍管霸與御史、廷尉雜考之。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor, receiving the memorial, was shaken with rage. He ordered the relevant offices to arrest Yun, decreeing that the Director of the Masters of Writing escort him with sword and halberd to the Northern Prison of the Yellow Gates, and sent Palace Attendant Guan Ba to examine him jointly with the Imperial Secretary and Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Emperor read the memorial and exploded with rage. He ordered Yun seized, had the Director of the Masters of Writing escort him under arms to the Northern Prison of the Yellow Gates, and set Palace Attendant Guan Ba to examine him together with the censor and the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時弘農五官掾杜眾傷雲以忠諫獲罪，上書「願與雲同日死」，帝愈怒，遂並下廷尉。

translations.literal: At this time Du Zhong, Senior Clerk for All Five Offices in Hongnong, grieved that Yun was punished for loyal remonstrance and submitted a memorial: "I wish to die on the same day as Yun." The Emperor grew still angrier and had them both sent to the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhong, a senior clerk in Hongnong, grieved that Yun was punished for honest counsel and wrote, "I wish to die on the same day as Yun." The Emperor's rage deepened, and both men were sent to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚陳蕃上疏曰：「李雲所言，雖不識禁忌，幹上逆旨，其意歸於忠國而已。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Chen Fan submitted a memorial, saying: "What Li Yun said, though ignorant of taboo and offensive to superiors and contrary to the imperial will, in intent amounted only to loyalty to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies Chen Fan memorialized: "Li Yun's words breached taboo and defied the throne, yet his intent was loyalty to the state alone.

sentences.zh: 昔高祖忍周昌不諱之諫，成帝赦朱雲腰領之誅，今日殺雲，臣恐剖心之譏，復議於世矣！

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Gaozu endured Zhou Chang's unreserved remonstrance; Emperor Cheng pardoned Zhu Yun from execution at the waist. If today Yun is killed, your servant fears the reproach of 'cutting out the heart' will again be debated in the world!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu once endured Zhou Chang's blunt counsel; Emperor Cheng spared Zhu Yun from beheading. Kill Yun today, and I fear the world will again speak of rulers who cut out loyal hearts!

sentences.zh: 」太常楊秉、雒陽市長沐茂、郎中上官資並上疏請雲。

translations.literal: 」Grand Master of Ceremonies Yang Bing, Market Chief of Luoyang Mu Mao, and Gentleman of the Palace Shangguan Zi all submitted memorials pleading for Yun.
translations.idiomatic: 」Grand Master of Ceremonies Yang Bing, Luoyang Market Chief Mu Mao, and Palace Gentleman Shangguan Zi all memorialized on Yun's behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝恚甚，有司奏以為大有敬。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly incensed. The relevant offices memorialized that this constituted great disrespect.
