translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious. Officials reported them for gross disrespect.

sentences.zh: 詔切責蕃、秉，免歸田裡，茂、資貶秩二等。

translations.literal: An edict sharply rebuked Fan and Bing and dismissed them to return to their home districts; Mao and Zi were demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sharply rebuked Fan and Bing and sent them home; Mao and Zi were demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 時帝在濯龍池，管霸奏雲等事，霸跪言曰：「李雲野澤愚儒，杜眾郡中小吏，出於狂戇，不足加罪。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor was at the Dragon-Washing Pool. Guan Ba reported on Yun and the others. Ba knelt and said: "Li Yun is a rustic fool of a scholar; Du Zhong is a petty clerk of a commandery. Their words sprang from rash stupidity and do not warrant punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was at the Dragon-Washing Pool when Guan Ba reported on the case. Ba knelt and said: "Li Yun is a rustic scholar; Du Zhong a county clerk. Their words were rash folly and merit no punishment.

sentences.zh: 」帝謂霸曰：「『帝欲不諦』，是何等語，而常侍欲原之邪！

translations.literal: 」The Emperor said to Ba: "'The emperor does not wish to listen closely'—what sort of words are these, and yet a Palace Attendant would pardon them!
translations.idiomatic: 」The Emperor said to Ba: "'The emperor does not wish to listen closely'—what kind of talk is that, and you would pardon them!

sentences.zh: 」顧使小黃門可其奏，雲、眾皆死獄中，於是嬖寵益橫。

translations.literal: 」He turned and had a Junior Palace Attendant approve the memorial. Yun and Zhong both died in prison. Thereupon the favored and pampered grew still more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: 」He had a Junior Palace Attendant ratify the verdict. Yun and Zhong died in prison, and the Emperor's favorites grew bolder than ever.

sentences.zh: 太尉瓊自度力不能制，乃稱疾不起，上疏曰：「陛下即位以來，未有勝政，諸梁秉權，豎宦充朝，李固、杜喬既以忠言橫見殘滅，而李雲、杜眾復以直道繼踵受誅，海內傷懼，益以怨結，朝野之人，以忠為諱。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Qiong, judging himself unable to restrain them, feigned illness and did not attend court. He submitted a memorial, saying: "Since Your Majesty's accession there has been no flourishing governance. The Liang clan wielded power; eunuchs fill the court. Li Gu and Du Qiao were already destroyed for loyal words, and now Li Yun and Du Zhong have in turn been executed for the straight path. Within the seas there is grief and fear, resentment ever mounting; men in court and countryside alike treat loyalty as a thing to be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Qiong, knowing he could not check them, feigned illness and stayed home. He memorialized: "Since Your Majesty's accession there has been no flourishing rule. The Liangs held power; eunuchs pack the court. Li Gu and Du Qiao were destroyed for honest counsel; Li Yun and Du Zhong followed them to execution. The realm grieves and fears; resentment mounts; court and country alike shun loyalty.

sentences.zh: 尚書周永，素事梁冀，假其威勢，見冀將衰，乃陽毀示忠，遂因奸計，亦取封侯。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Zhou Yong had long served Liang Ji and borrowed his power and influence. Seeing Ji about to fall, he feigned denunciation to show loyalty and, through a treacherous scheme, also obtained enfeoffment as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Zhou Yong had long served Liang Ji and traded on his power. Seeing Ji's fall approaching, he pretended to denounce him, plotted his way into favor, and won a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 又，黃門挾邪，群輩相黨，自冀興盛，腹背相親，朝夕圖謀，共構奸軌；

translations.literal: Moreover, the Yellow Gates clung to wickedness; factions banded together. From Ji's rise they were intimate as belly and back, plotting morning and evening, jointly weaving treacherous designs;
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Gate eunuchs clung to evil and formed factions. From Ji's ascendancy they were inseparable, plotting day and night, weaving treachery together;

sentences.zh: 臨冀當誅，無可設巧，復記其惡以要爵賞。

translations.literal: When Ji was about to be executed they could devise no stratagem, so they recorded his crimes to demand titles and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was doomed they could play no clever game, so they recorded his crimes to claim titles and rewards.

sentences.zh: 陛下不加清征，審別真偽，復與忠臣並時顯封，使朱紫共色，粉墨雜糅，所謂抵金玉於沙礫，碎珪璧於泥塗，四方聞之，莫不憤歎。

translations.literal: Your Majesty did not conduct a clear investigation or distinguish true from false, but again enfeoffed them alongside loyal ministers at the same time, making crimson and purple of one hue and mixing powder and ink—the so-called casting gold and jade among sand and gravel, shattering scepter-jades in the mud. When the four quarters heard of it, none failed to rage and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty did not investigate or separate true from false, but enfeoffed them alongside loyal ministers, making crimson and purple indistinguishable, jade and chalk alike—the proverb of casting gold among gravel and shattering scepters in mud. All the realm raged and lamented.

sentences.zh: 臣世荷國恩，身輕位重，敢以垂絕之日，陳不諱之言。

translations.literal: Your servant's family has received the state's grace for generations; though the body is slight, the office is weighty. I dare, on the verge of death, to speak words without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: My family has owed the state for generations. Though I am insignificant, my office is weighty. On the edge of death I dare speak without reserve.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，不納。

translations.literal: 」The memorial was submitted and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: 」The memorial was ignored.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬申，上行幸長安。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day renshen, the Emperor traveled in state to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on renshen day, the Emperor traveled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 中常侍單超疾病；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Shan Chao fell ill;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Shan Chao fell ill;

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以超為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Chao was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day, Chao was made General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己巳，上還自長安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day jisi, the Emperor returned from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jisi day, the Emperor returned from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 燒當、燒何、當煎、勒姐等八種羌寇隴西金城塞，護羌校尉段穎擊破之，追至羅亭，斬其酋豪以下二千級，獲生口萬餘人。

translations.literal: Eight Qiang tribes including Shaodang, Shaohe, Dangjian, and Lejie raided the passes of Longxi and Jincheng. Protector of the Qiang Duan Yong defeated them, pursued to Luoting, beheaded chieftains and others to the number of two thousand, and captured more than ten thousand living captives.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Qiang tribes—Shaodang, Shaohe, Dangjian, Lejie, and others—raided the Longxi and Jincheng frontier. Protector of the Qiang Duan Yong routed them, pursued them to Luoting, took two thousand heads including chieftains, and captured more than ten thousand people.

sentences.zh: 詔復以陳蕃為光祿勳，楊秉為河南尹。

translations.literal: An edict restored Chen Fan as Director of the Masters of the Imperial Luminaries and Yang Bing as Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Chen Fan as Director of the Imperial Luminaries and made Yang Bing Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 單超兄子匡為濟陰太守，負勢貪放。

translations.literal: Shan Chao's brother's son Kuang was Administrator of Jiyin, relying on influence and greedy and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Chao's nephew Kuang was Administrator of Jiyin, abusing his family's power with greed and license.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史第五種使從事衛羽案之，得臧五六千萬，種即奏匡，並以劾超。

translations.literal: Yan Province Inspector Diwu Zhong sent Attendant Wei Yu to investigate him and found embezzled goods of fifty or sixty million. Zhong immediately memorialized against Kuang and also impeached Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Province Inspector Diwu Zhong sent Attendant Wei Yu to investigate and uncovered embezzlement of fifty or sixty million. Zhong memorialized against Kuang and impeached Chao as well.

sentences.zh: 匡窘迫，賂客任方刺羽。

translations.literal: Kuang, cornered, bribed a retainer Ren Fang to assassinate Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Kuang bribed a retainer, Ren Fang, to kill Yu.

sentences.zh: 羽覺其奸，捕方，囚系雒陽。

translations.literal: Yu perceived the treachery, seized Fang, and imprisoned him in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu saw through the plot, seized Fang, and imprisoned him in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 匡慮楊秉窮竟其事，密令方等突獄亡走。

translations.literal: Kuang feared Yang Bing would pursue the matter to the end and secretly ordered Fang and others to break prison and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yang Bing would pursue the case to its end, Kuang secretly ordered Fang and others to break out of prison and flee.

sentences.zh: 尚書召秉詰責，秉對曰：「方等無狀，釁由單匡，乞檻車征匡，考核其事，則奸慝蹤緒，必可立得。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing summoned Bing to rebuke him. Bing replied: "Fang and the others are worthless; the provocation came from Shan Kuang. I beg that Kuang be summoned in a caged cart to examine the matter—then the tracks of treachery and greed can surely be found at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing summoned Bing for rebuke. Bing replied: "Fang and his ilk are worthless; the trouble began with Shan Kuang. Summon Kuang in a prison cart and investigate—then the trail of treachery and greed will quickly appear.

sentences.zh: 」秉竟坐論作左校。

translations.literal: 」Bing in the end was convicted and sentenced to service in the Left Construction Corps.
translations.idiomatic: 」Bing was convicted and sentenced to the Left Construction Corps.

sentences.zh: 時泰山賊叔孫無忌寇暴徐、兗，州郡不能討，單超以是陷第五種，坐徙朔方；

translations.literal: At this time the Taishan bandit Shusun Wuji raided and ravaged Xu and Yan provinces; the provinces and commanderies could not suppress him. Shan Chao used this to entrap Diwu Zhong, who was sentenced to exile in Shuofang;
translations.idiomatic: The Taishan bandit Shusun Wuji ravaged Xu and Yan; local authorities could not suppress him. Shan Chao used this to frame Diwu Zhong, who was exiled to Shuofang;

sentences.zh: 超外孫董援為朔方太守，蓄怒以待之。

translations.literal: Chao's daughter's son Dong Yuan was Administrator of Shuofang, storing up wrath to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's grandson Dong Yuan was Administrator of Shuofang, nursing his rage in wait for Zhong.

sentences.zh: 種故吏孫斌知種必死，結客追種，及於太原，劫之以歸，亡命數年，會赦得免。

translations.literal: Zhong's former clerk Sun Bin knew Zhong would surely die. He gathered clients, pursued Zhong, caught up with him at Taiyuan, seized him and carried him off, and they were outlaws for several years until an amnesty spared them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's former clerk Sun Bin knew Zhong would die. He gathered men, overtook Zhong at Taiyuan, abducted him, and they lived as fugitives for years until an amnesty saved them.

sentences.zh: 種，倫之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zhong was the great-grandson of Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was the great-grandson of Lun.

sentences.zh: 是時，封賞逾制，內寵猥盛。

translations.literal: At this time enfeoffments and rewards exceeded regulation, and inner favorites were excessively numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffments and rewards now exceeded all precedent, and the Emperor's inner favorites proliferated.

sentences.zh: 陳蕃上疏曰：「夫諸侯上象四七，籓屏上國；

translations.literal: Chen Fan submitted a memorial, saying: "Marquisates correspond above to the twenty-eight lunar mansions and serve as screens for the upper state;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fan memorialized: "Marquisates mirror the twenty-eight mansions above and shield the realm;

sentences.zh: 高祖之約，非功臣不侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu's covenant: none but meritorious ministers are enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu's covenant held that only meritorious ministers could be enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 而聞追錄河南尹鄧萬世父遵之微功，更爵尚書令黃俊先人之絕封。

translations.literal: Yet I hear that the slight merit of Deng Wanshi's father Zun is being traced and recorded, and Director of the Masters of Writing Huang Jun's ancestor's extinguished enfeoffment is being restored.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear Deng Wanshi's father Zun is being enfeoffed for slight merit, and Director Huang Jun's ancestor's lapsed title restored.

sentences.zh: 近習以非義授邑，左右以無功傳賞，至乃一門之內，侯者數人，故緯象失度，陰陽謬序。

translations.literal: Close favorites receive fiefs without justice; those at hand pass down rewards without merit—so that within a single gate several may be marquises. Thus the weft-stars lose their measure and yin and yang fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Favorites receive fiefs unjustly; courtiers inherit rewards without merit—several marquises under one roof. No wonder the heavens lose their measure and yin and yang fall out of order.

sentences.zh: 臣知封事已行，言之無及，誠欲陛下從是而止。

translations.literal: Your servant knows the enfeoffments are already done and speech comes too late; I truly wish Your Majesty would stop from here.
translations.idiomatic: The enfeoffments are done and words come too late; I ask only that Your Majesty stop here.

sentences.zh: 又，采女數千，食肉衣綺，脂油粉黛，不可貲計。

translations.literal: Moreover, palace women number in the thousands, eating meat and wearing brocade; grease, powder, and rouge cannot be reckoned in value.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women number in the thousands, feasting on meat and draped in silk; oils, powders, and cosmetics beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 鄙諺言『盜不過五女門』，以女貧家也；

translations.literal: A vulgar proverb says, 'A thief does not pass a gate with five daughters,' because daughters impoverish a household;
translations.idiomatic: A folk saying runs, 'Thieves skip houses with five daughters,' for daughters beggar a home;

sentences.zh: 今後宮之女，豈不貧國乎！

translations.literal: Are not the women of the inner palace beggaring the state!
translations.idiomatic: Are the women of the inner palace not beggaring the state!

sentences.zh: 」帝頗采其言，為出宮女五百餘人，但賜俊爵關內侯，而封萬世南鄉侯。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor largely adopted his words and released more than five hundred palace women, but only enfeoffed Jun as Marquis Within the Passes and enfeoffed Wanshi as Marquis of Nanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Emperor took much of this to heart and released more than five hundred palace women—but still made Jun Marquis Within the Passes and Wanshi Marquis of Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 帝從容問侍中陳留爰延：「朕何如主也？

translations.literal: The Emperor casually asked Palace Attendant Yuan Yan of Chenliu: "What sort of ruler am I?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor casually asked Palace Attendant Yuan Yan of Chenliu: "What sort of ruler am I?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下為漢中主。

translations.literal: 」He replied: "Your Majesty is a middling ruler of Han.
translations.idiomatic: 」He replied: "Your Majesty is a middling ruler of Han.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「何以言之？

translations.literal: 」The Emperor said: "By what do you say so?
translations.idiomatic: 」The Emperor said: "How so?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「尚書令陳蕃任事則治，中常侍黃門與政則亂。

translations.literal: 」He replied: "When Director of the Masters of Writing Chen Fan handles affairs, there is order; when Palace Attendants and Yellow Gates participate in government, there is disorder.
translations.idiomatic: 」He replied: "When Chen Fan as Director of the Masters of Writing takes charge, there is order; when eunuchs meddle in government, there is chaos.

sentences.zh: 是以知陛下可與為善，可與為非。

translations.literal: Hence I know Your Majesty can be led to do good or led to do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Hence I know Your Majesty can be steered toward good or toward ill.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「昔朱雲廷折欄檻，今侍中面稱朕違，敬聞闕矣。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor said: "Formerly Zhu Yun broke the courtyard balustrade in open court; now a Palace Attendant to my face calls me in error—I respectfully accept the reproof.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Emperor said: "Zhu Yun once broke the balustrade remonstrating in open court; now a Palace Attendant tells me to my face I am wrong—I hear the rebuke and accept it.

sentences.zh: 」拜五官中郎將，累遷大鴻臚。

translations.literal: 」He was appointed General of the Five Offices and promoted in succession to Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: 」Yan was made General of the Five Offices and eventually rose to Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 會客星經帝坐，帝密以問延，延上封事曰：「陛下以河南尹鄧萬世有龍潛之舊，封為通侯，恩重公卿，惠豐宗室；

translations.literal: When a guest star crossed the Emperor's throne, the Emperor secretly questioned Yan. Yan submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "Your Majesty, because Intendant of Henan Deng Wanshi shared your days of hidden dragonhood, enfeoffed him as a full marquis, with grace outweighing the Three Excellencies and favor enriching the imperial clan;
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star crossed the imperial throne, the Emperor quietly consulted Yan. Yan submitted a sealed memorial: "Your Majesty enfeoffed Intendant of Henan Deng Wanshi as a full marquis for old companionship in your days before the throne, honoring him above the Three Excellencies and enriching the clan;

sentences.zh: 加頃引見，與之對博，上下□葉黷，有虧尊嚴。

translations.literal: Recently summoning him for audience and playing dice together, superior and inferior in frivolous intimacy, there was injury to dignity.
translations.idiomatic: You recently received him in audience and played dice together—frivolous intimacy between sovereign and subject that diminished your dignity.

sentences.zh: 臣聞之，帝左右者，所以咨政德也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that those at the Emperor's side are for consulting on governance and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Those at the Emperor's side exist to counsel on governance and virtue.

sentences.zh: 善人同處，則日聞嘉訓；

translations.literal: Dwell with good men and daily one hears fine instruction;
translations.idiomatic: Keep good company and you hear fine counsel each day;

sentences.zh: 惡人從游，則日生邪情。

translations.literal: Follow and roam with wicked men and daily wicked sentiments arise.
translations.idiomatic: Keep wicked company and corrupt impulses grow daily.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下遠讒諛之人，納謇謇之士，則災變可除。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty keeps distant slanderers and flatterers and accepts upright, outspoken scholars can portents be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Distance slanderers and flatterers; welcome blunt, upright men—and the portents may be dispelled.

sentences.zh: 」帝不能用。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Emperor did not heed it.

sentences.zh: 延稱病，免歸。

translations.literal: Yan claimed illness and was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Yan pleaded illness and was sent home.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙申，赦天下，詔求李固後嗣。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day bingshen, there was an amnesty for all under heaven, and an edict sought descendants of Li Gu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on bingshen day, an empire-wide amnesty was proclaimed and an edict sought descendants of Li Gu.

sentences.zh: 初，固既策罷，知不免禍，乃遣三子基、茲、燮皆歸鄉里，時燮年十三，姊文姬為同郡趙伯英妻，見二兄歸，具知事本，默然獨悲曰：「李氏滅矣！

translations.literal: Initially, after Gu was removed by imperial rescript, knowing he could not escape disaster, he sent his three sons Ji, Zi, and Xie all back to their home district. At that time Xie was thirteen. His elder sister Wenji was wife of Zhao Boying of the same commandery. Seeing her two brothers return, she knew the whole matter and silently grieved alone, saying: "The house of Li is destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: When Gu was dismissed by rescript, knowing disaster was inevitable, he sent his three sons Ji, Zi, and Xie home. Xie was thirteen. His sister Wenji, wife of Zhao Boying in the same commandery, saw her brothers return, understood everything, and murmured in grief: "The house of Li is finished!

sentences.zh: 自太公已來，積德累仁，何以遇此！

translations.literal: From Lord Tai onward, accumulating virtue and heaping benevolence—how do we meet this!
translations.idiomatic: From Lord Tai onward we heaped virtue upon virtue—how did we come to this!

sentences.zh: 」密與二兄謀，豫藏匿燮，託言還京師，人咸信之。

translations.literal: 」Secretly she plotted with her two brothers, beforehand hiding Xie and putting it about that he had returned to the capital—all believed it.
translations.idiomatic: 」She secretly plotted with her brothers, hid Xie in advance, and spread word that he had returned to the capital. All believed it.

sentences.zh: 有頃，難作，州郡收基、茲，皆死獄中。

translations.literal: Before long calamity struck. The province and commandery seized Ji and Zi; both died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon disaster struck. Authorities seized Ji and Zi; both died in prison.

sentences.zh: 文姬乃告父門生王成曰：「君執義先公，有古人之節；

translations.literal: Wenji then told her father's student Wang Cheng: "You upheld righteousness for my late father and have the integrity of the ancients;
translations.idiomatic: Wenji then told her father's student Wang Cheng: "You served my father with integrity, with the honor of the ancients;

sentences.zh: 今委君以六尺之孤，李氏存滅，其在君矣！

translations.literal: Now I entrust to you a six-foot orphan—the survival or extinction of the house of Li rests with you!
translations.idiomatic: I entrust to you a fatherless child—the survival of the house of Li rests with you!

sentences.zh: 」成乃將燮乘江東下，入徐州界，變姓名為酒家傭，而成賣卜於市，各為異人，陰相往來。

translations.literal: 」Cheng then took Xie downstream east of the river into Xu Province, changed their names—Xie as a tavern servant and Cheng selling divination in the market—each posing as a stranger while secretly keeping contact.
translations.idiomatic: 」Cheng took Xie downriver into Xu Province. Xie became a tavern hand under a false name; Cheng sold divinations in the market. They passed as strangers but kept in secret contact.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，梁冀既誅，燮乃以本末告酒家，酒傢具車重厚遣之，燮皆不受，遂還鄉里，追行喪服，姊弟相見，悲感傍人。

translations.literal: After more than ten years, once Liang Ji was executed, Xie told the tavern keeper the whole story. The tavern keeper prepared a carriage and rich gifts to send him off; Xie refused all and returned to his home district, resumed mourning garb, and brother and sister met—grief that moved all who saw them.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years, once Liang Ji was dead, Xie confided in the tavern keeper, who offered a carriage and rich gifts. Xie refused, returned home, put on mourning, and met his sister— their grief moved all who watched.

sentences.zh: 姊戒燮曰：「吾家血食將絕，弟幸而得濟，豈非天邪！

translations.literal: His sister admonished Xie: "Our family's sacrificial line is nearly cut. Younger brother, you were spared by fortune—is this not Heaven's doing!
translations.idiomatic: His sister warned him: "Our ancestral sacrifices nearly ended; you were spared by fortune—is this not Heaven's will!

sentences.zh: 宜杜絕眾人，勿妄往來，慎無一言加於梁氏！

translations.literal: You should cut off contact with the crowd, make no reckless comings and goings, and be careful never to speak a word against the Liang clan!
translations.idiomatic: Cut yourself off from others, wander nowhere recklessly, and never breathe a word against the Liangs!

sentences.zh: 加梁氏則連主上，禍重至矣，唯引咎而已。

translations.literal: To implicate the Liang clan is to implicate the sovereign—disaster would come again. Only take blame upon yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Implicate the Liangs and you implicate the Emperor—disaster would return. Blame only yourself.

sentences.zh: 」燮謹從其誨。

translations.literal: 」Xie carefully followed her instruction.
translations.idiomatic: 」Xie obeyed her counsel faithfully.

sentences.zh: 後王成卒，燮以禮葬之，每四節為設上賓之位而祠焉。

translations.literal: Later Wang Cheng died. Xie buried him with full rites and at each of the four seasonal festivals set out the seat of chief guest and made offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Cheng died, Xie buried him with full rites and at each seasonal festival set a chief guest's seat and made offerings.

sentences.zh: 丙午，新豐侯單超卒，賜東園秘器，棺中玉具；

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Marquis of Xinfeng Shan Chao died. He was granted secret funerary vessels of the Eastern Garden and jade fittings for the coffin;
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day, Marquis of Xinfeng Shan Chao died. He received the Eastern Garden's secret funerary regalia and jade coffin fittings;

sentences.zh: 及葬，發五營騎士、將作大匠起塚塋。

translations.literal: At the burial, five-camp horsemen were mobilized and the Master of Construction raised his tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: At his burial, cavalry from the five camps were mobilized and the Master of Construction raised his tomb.

sentences.zh: 其後四侯轉橫，天下為之語曰：「左回天，具獨坐，徐臥虎，唐雨墮。

translations.literal: Thereafter the four marquises grew still more overbearing. The realm made a saying of them: "Zuo turns back heaven, Ju sits alone, Xu sleeps like a tiger, Tang falls like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The four remaining marquises grew bolder still. People said of them: "Zuo turns back heaven, Ju sits alone, Xu the crouching tiger, Tang falling rain.

sentences.zh: 」皆競起第宅，以華侈相尚，其僕從皆乘牛車而從列騎，兄弟姻戚，宰州臨郡，辜較百姓，與盜無異，虐遍天下；

translations.literal: 」All vied to raise mansions, competing in splendor and extravagance. Their servants and followers rode ox-carts while escorted by ranks of horsemen; brothers and in-laws held provinces and faced commanderies, squeezing the common people no differently from bandits, cruelty spreading through the realm;
translations.idiomatic: 」They vied in building mansions, outdoing one another in luxury. Servants rode ox-carts flanked by cavalry; brothers and in-laws governed provinces and squeezed the people like bandits, cruelty spreading everywhere;

sentences.zh: 民不堪命，故多為盜賊焉。

translations.literal: The people could not bear their lives; therefore many became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The people could not endure it, and many turned to banditry.

sentences.zh: 中常侍侯覽，小黃門段珪，皆有田業近濟北界，僕從賓客，劫掠行旅。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Hou Lan and Junior Palace Attendant Duan Gui both had estates near the Jibei border; servants, followers, and guests plundered travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Hou Lan and Junior Palace Attendant Duan Gui held estates near Jibei; their servants and guests robbed travelers.

sentences.zh: 濟北相滕延，一切收捕，殺數十人，陳屍路衢。

translations.literal: Chancellor of Jibei Teng Yan seized them all, killed several tens, and displayed corpses in the public roads.
translations.idiomatic: Jibei Chancellor Teng Yan arrested them wholesale, killed dozens, and lined the roads with corpses.

sentences.zh: 覽、珪以事訴帝，延坐征詣廷尉，免。

translations.literal: Lan and Gui complained to the Emperor about the matter. Yan was convicted, summoned to the Commandant of Justice, and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Lan and Gui appealed to the Emperor. Yan was convicted, summoned to the Commandant of Justice, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 左心官兄勝為河東太守，皮氏長京兆岐恥之，即日棄官西歸。

translations.literal: Zuo Xinguan's elder brother Sheng was Administrator of Hedong. Qi of Jingzhao, magistrate of Pishi, was shamed by this and the same day abandoned office and returned west.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Xinguan's brother Sheng was Administrator of Hedong. Qi of Jingzhao, magistrate of Pishi, was shamed and quit his post that same day to return west.

sentences.zh: 唐衡兄玹為京兆尹，素與岐有隙，收岐家屬宗親，陷以重法，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Tang Heng's elder brother Xuan was Intendant of Jingzhao. He had long borne a grudge against Qi, seized Qi's family and clan, trapped them with heavy penalties, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Heng's brother Xuan was Intendant of Jingzhao. Long at odds with Qi, he seized Qi's family and kin, condemned them under harsh law, and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 岐逃難四方，靡所不歷，自匿姓名，賣餅北海市中；

translations.literal: Qi fled through the four quarters, nowhere he did not pass, hid his name, and sold cakes in the market of Beihai;
translations.idiomatic: Qi fled everywhere, hiding his name and selling cakes in the Beihai market;

sentences.zh: 安丘孫嵩見而異之，載與俱歸，藏於復壁中。

translations.literal: Sun Song of Anqiu saw him and found him strange, took him in his carriage and returned together, and hid him in a hollow wall.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Song of Anqiu noticed him, took him home in his carriage, and hid him in a secret wall compartment.

sentences.zh: 及諸唐死，遇赦，乃敢出。

translations.literal: When the Tang clan died out and he met an amnesty, only then did he dare emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang clan was gone and an amnesty came, he dared emerge at last.

sentences.zh: 閏月，西羌餘眾復與燒何大豪寇張掖，晨，薄校尉段熲軍。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Western Qiang remnant bands again joined the Shaohe chieftain in raiding Zhangye. At dawn they pressed upon Colonel Duan Yong's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Western Qiang remnants joined the Shaohe chieftain in raiding Zhangye. At dawn they closed on Colonel Duan Yong's camp.

sentences.zh: 熲下馬大戰，至日中，刀折矢盡，虜亦引退。

translations.literal: Yong dismounted for fierce battle. By midday swords were broken and arrows exhausted; the barbarians also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yong dismounted to fight hand to hand. By midday his blades were broken and his quiver empty; the enemy withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 熲追之，且鬥且行，晝夜相攻，割肉食雪，四十餘日，遂至積石山，出塞二千餘里，斬燒何大帥，降其餘眾而還。

translations.literal: Yong pursued them, fighting as he marched, attacking day and night, cutting flesh and eating snow. After more than forty days he reached Jishi Mountain, went beyond the frontier more than two thousand li, beheaded the Shaohe grand chieftain, accepted the surrender of the rest, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yong pursued, fighting by day and marching by night, gnawing raw flesh and snow. After forty-odd days he reached Jishi Mountain, crossed two thousand li beyond the frontier, killed the Shaohe chieftain, accepted the surrender of the rest, and returned.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，甲戌，漢中山崩。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day jiaxu, Mount Zhong of Han collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on jiaxu day, Mount Zhong in Han collapsed.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛丑，司徒祝恬薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day xinchou, Minister over the Masses Zhu Tian died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinchou day, Minister over the Masses Zhu Tian died.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以司空盛允為司徒，太常虞放為司空。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Minister of Works Sheng Yun was made Minister over the Masses, and Grand Master of Ceremonies Yu Fang was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Sheng Yun was promoted from Minister of Works to Minister over the Masses, and Yu Fang from Grand Master of Ceremonies to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 長沙蠻反，屯益陽，零陵蠻寇長沙。

translations.literal: Changsha Man rebelled and encamped at Yiyang; Lingling Man raided Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: The Changsha tribes rebelled and camped at Yiyang; Lingling tribes raided Changsha.

sentences.zh: 九真餘賊屯據日南，眾轉強盛；

translations.literal: Remnant bandits of Jiuzhen occupied and held Rinan; their numbers grew ever stronger;
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhen remnant rebels held Rinan, and their strength grew;

sentences.zh: 詔復拜桂陽太守夏方為交趾刺史。

translations.literal: An edict again appointed Administrator of Guiyang Xia Fang as Inspector of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reappointed Guiyang Administrator Xia Fang as Inspector of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 方威惠素著，冬，十一月，日南賊二萬餘人相率詣方降。

translations.literal: Fang's authority and kindness had long been renowned. In winter, the eleventh month, more than twenty thousand bandits of Rinan in succession came to Fang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's authority and kindness were well known. In winter, in the eleventh month, more than twenty thousand Rinan rebels came in succession to surrender to him.

sentences.zh: 勒姐、零吾種羌圍允街；

translations.literal: Lejie and Lingwu Qiang tribes besieged Yunjie;
translations.idiomatic: Lejie and Lingwu Qiang tribes besieged Yunjie;

sentences.zh: 段熲擊破之。

translations.literal: Duan Yong defeated and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yong routed them.

sentences.zh: 泰山賊叔孫無忌攻殺都尉侯章；

translations.literal: The Taishan bandit Shusun Wuji attacked and killed Commandant Hou Zhang;
translations.idiomatic: The Taishan bandit Shusun Wuji attacked and killed Commandant Hou Zhang;

sentences.zh: 遣中郎將宗資討破之。

translations.literal: A General of the Gentlemen of the Palace Zong Zi was sent to campaign against and defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Gentlemen of the Palace Zong Zi was dispatched and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 詔征皇甫規，拜泰山太守。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Huangfu Gui and appointed him Administrator of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Huangfu Gui and made him Administrator of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 規到官，廣設方略，寇虜悉平。

translations.literal: When Gui reached his post, he broadly deployed stratagems and the raiding barbarians were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Gui took office, laid broad plans, and pacified the raiders completely.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉，南宮嘉德殿火；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinyou, the Jiade Hall of the Southern Palace burned;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on xinyou day, the Jiade Hall of the Southern Palace burned;

sentences.zh: 戊子，丙署火。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, the Bing Office burned.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day, the Bing Office burned.

sentences.zh: 大疫。

translations.literal: A great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: A great pestilence struck.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬辰，武庫火。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day renchen, the armory burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renchen day, the armory burned.

sentences.zh: 司徒盛允免，以大司農種暠為司徒。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Sheng Yun was dismissed; Grand Minister of Agriculture Zhong Hao was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Sheng Yun was dismissed and Grand Minister of Agriculture Zhong Hao appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 三月，太尉黃瓊免；

translations.literal: In the third month, Grand Commandant Huang Qiong was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Grand Commandant Huang Qiong was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以太常沛國劉矩為太尉。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Ju of Pei was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Ju of Pei was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 初，矩為雍丘令，以禮讓化民；

translations.literal: Initially, when Ju was magistrate of Yongqiu, he transformed the people through ritual and yielding;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as magistrate of Yongqiu, Ju civilized the people through courtesy and forbearance;

sentences.zh: 有訟者，常引之於前，提耳訓告，以為忿恚可忍，縣官不可入，使歸更思。

translations.literal: When there were litigants, he would often bring them before him, pull their ears and instruct them, saying that anger could be endured but the magistrate's office could not be entered, and send them home to reconsider.
translations.idiomatic: When people came to sue, he drew them close, tugged their ears, and admonished them: anger can be borne, but the magistrate's court cannot be entered lightly—go home and think again.

sentences.zh: 訟者感之，輒各罷去。

translations.literal: The litigants were moved and each withdrew their suits.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the litigants withdrew their suits.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，封河間孝王子參戶亭侯博為任城王，奉孝王后。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Canhu Precinct Marquis Bo, son of King Xiao of Hejian, was enfeoffed as King of Rencheng to continue the line of King Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day, Canhu Precinct Marquis Bo, son of King Xiao of Hejian, was enfeoffed as King of Rencheng to continue the late king's line.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛酉，有星孛於心。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day xinyou, a broom star appeared in the Heart constellation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinyou day, a comet appeared in the Heart constellation.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，原陵長壽門火。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, the Longevity Gate of Yuanling burned.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day, the Longevity Gate of Yuanling burned.

sentences.zh: 己卯，京師雨雹。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, the capital rained hail.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day, hail fell on the capital.

sentences.zh: 六月，京兆、扶風及涼州地震。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Jingzhao, Fufeng, and Liang Province were shaken by earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Jingzhao, Fufeng, and Liang Province were struck by earthquake.

sentences.zh: 庚子，岱山及博尤來山並頹裂。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Mount Dai and Mount Boyou both collapsed and split.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day, Mount Dai and Mount Boyou both collapsed.

sentences.zh: 己酉，赦天下。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, there was an amnesty for all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day, an empire-wide amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 司空虞放免，以前太尉黃瓊為司空。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yu Fang was dismissed; former Grand Commandant Huang Qiong was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yu Fang was dismissed and former Grand Commandant Huang Qiong appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 犍為屬國夷寇鈔百姓。

translations.literal: Yi of the Dependent State of Jianwei raided and plundered the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes of the Jianwei Dependent State raided and plundered the people.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史山昱擊破之。

translations.literal: Yi Province Inspector Shan Yu defeated and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Province Inspector Shan Yu routed them.

sentences.zh: 零吾羌與先零諸種反，寇三輔。

translations.literal: Lingwu Qiang together with various Xianling tribes rebelled and raided the Three Adjuncts.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwu Qiang and various Xianling tribes rebelled and raided the Three Adjuncts.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，京師雩。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the capital held a rain sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, the capital held a rain sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 減公卿已下奉，貣王侯半租，占賣關內侯、虎賁、羽林緹騎、營士、五大夫錢各有差。

translations.literal: Salaries of Excellencies and below were reduced; kings and marquises were lent half their rent; prices for purchasing by lottery ranks of Marquis Within the Passes, Tiger Guards, Forest Guards, mounted escorts, camp soldiers, and Grandee of the Fifth Order were set at various levels.
translations.idiomatic: Salaries of officials below the Excellencies were cut; kings and marquises were lent half their rents; offices from Marquis Within the Passes down to Grandee of the Fifth Order were sold by lottery at set prices.

sentences.zh: 九月，司空黃瓊免，以大鴻臚東萊劉寵為司空。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Minister of Works Huang Qiong was dismissed; Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Chong of Donglai was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Huang Qiong was dismissed as Minister of Works and Liu Chong of Donglai, Grand Master of Ceremonies, took his place.

sentences.zh: 寵常為會稽太守，簡除煩苛，禁察非法，郡中大治；

translations.literal: Chong had formerly been Administrator of Kuaiji, simplifying and removing burdensome harshness, forbidding and investigating illegal acts—the commandery was greatly governed;
translations.idiomatic: Chong had served as Administrator of Kuaiji, cutting red tape, forbidding abuses—the commandery flourished;

sentences.zh: 征為將作大匠。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Master of Construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to be Master of Construction.

sentences.zh: 山陰縣有五六老叟，自若邪山谷間出，人繼百錢以送寵曰：「山谷鄙生，未嘗識郡朝，它守時，吏發求民間，至夜不絕，或狗吠竟夕，民不得安。

translations.literal: In Shanyin County five or six old men came out from the valleys of Ruye. Each in succession gave a hundred cash to send Chong off, saying: "We crude folk of the valleys have never known the commandery court. Under other administrators, officials were sent to demand from the people without cease even into the night; sometimes dogs barked the whole evening and the people could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: Five or six old men of Shanyin County came from the Ruye valleys, each offering a hundred cash to see Chong off: "We hill folk never knew the commandery seat. Under other administrators officials plundered the people day and night; dogs barked till dawn and no one rested.

sentences.zh: 自明府下車以來，狗不夜吠，民不見吏；

translations.literal: Since Your Excellency took office, dogs do not bark at night and the people do not see officials;
translations.idiomatic: Since you took office, dogs no longer bark at night and the people never see officials;

sentences.zh: 年老遭值聖明，今聞當見棄去，故自扶奉送。

translations.literal: We old men have met a sage and enlightened age; now hearing you are to be cast aside, we therefore support one another to come and send you off.
translations.idiomatic: We old men have lived to see an enlightened age; hearing you are leaving, we came on our own to see you off.

sentences.zh: 」寵曰：「吾政何能及公言邪！

translations.literal: 」Chong said: "How can my governance reach what you say!
translations.idiomatic: 」Chong said: "My governance hardly deserves such praise!

sentences.zh: 勤苦父老！

translations.literal: You toil, aged sirs!
translations.idiomatic: You honor me, old sirs!

sentences.zh: 」為人選一大錢受之。

translations.literal: 」From each person he selected one large coin and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: 」From each he accepted a single large coin.

sentences.zh: 冬，先零、沈氐羌與諸種羌寇並、涼二州，校尉段熲將湟中義從討之。

translations.literal: In winter, Xianling, Shenshi, and various Qiang tribes raided Bing and Liang provinces. Colonel Duan Yong led volunteer allies from Huangzhong to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, Xianling, Shenshi, and other Qiang tribes raided Bing and Liang. Colonel Duan Yong led Huangzhong volunteers against them.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史郭閎貪共其功，稽固熲軍，使不得進；

translations.literal: Liang Province Inspector Guo Hong greedily wished to share the merit, detained and held Yong's army, and would not let it advance;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Inspector Guo Hong, greedy for credit, detained Yong's army and blocked its advance;

sentences.zh: 義從役久戀鄉舊，皆悉叛歸。

translations.literal: The volunteer allies, long in service and longing for home, all rebelled and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The volunteers, weary and homesick, all deserted and went home.

sentences.zh: 郭閎歸罪於熲，熲坐征下獄，輸作左校，以濟南相胡閎代為校尉。

translations.literal: Guo Hong shifted blame onto Yong. Yong was convicted, summoned, and imprisoned, sentenced to service in the Left Construction Corps; Administrator of Jinan Hu Hong replaced him as Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Hong blamed Yong. Yong was arrested, sentenced to the Left Construction Corps, and Jinan Administrator Hu Hong replaced him as Protector.

sentences.zh: 胡閎無威略，羌遂陸梁，覆沒營塢，轉相招結，唐突諸郡，寇患轉盛。

translations.literal: Hu Hong had no authority or strategy. The Qiang therefore grew unruly, overran camps and fortresses, linked up with one another, stormed various commanderies, and the raiding menace grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Hong lacked authority and strategy. The Qiang grew bold, overran forts, joined forces, and stormed commanderies—the threat worsened.

sentences.zh: 泰山太守皇甫規上疏曰：「今猾賊就滅，泰山略平，復聞群羌並皆反逆。

translations.literal: Administrator of Taishan Huangfu Gui submitted a memorial, saying: "Now the cunning bandits are nearly extinguished and Taishan is largely pacified, yet I again hear that the Qiang tribes have all rebelled together.
translations.idiomatic: Taishan Administrator Huangfu Gui memorialized: "The bandits are nearly gone and Taishan largely pacified, yet the Qiang have rebelled en masse.

sentences.zh: 臣生長邠岐，年五十有九，昔為郡吏，再更叛羌，豫籌其事，有誤中之言。

translations.literal: Your servant grew up in Bin and Qi, is fifty-nine years old, was once a commandery clerk, twice experienced Qiang rebellion, and foresaw the matter—there were words that hit the mark by mistake.
translations.idiomatic: I grew up on the Bin-Qi frontier, am fifty-nine, served as a commandery clerk, and twice weathered Qiang revolts—I foresaw this crisis and spoke of it before.

sentences.zh: 臣素有痼疾，恐犬馬齒窮，不報大恩，願乞冗官，備單車一介之使，勞來三輔，宣國威澤，以所習地形兵勢佐助諸軍。

translations.literal: Your servant has long had a chronic illness and fears my dog-and-horse years will run out without repaying great grace. I wish to beg a supernumerary office, to serve as envoy with a single cart, to comfort the Three Adjuncts, proclaim the state's authority and favor, and with terrain and military disposition I know assist the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: I am chronically ill and fear my years are running out before I repay the state. Grant me a humble post—a lone envoy's cart—to comfort the Three Adjuncts, proclaim imperial authority, and lend the terrain and tactics I know to our armies.

sentences.zh: 臣窮居孤危之中，坐觀郡將已數十年，自鳥鼠至於東岱，其病一也。

translations.literal: Your servant dwells in poverty and isolation in peril, sitting and watching commandery generals for decades—from Bird-and-Rat to Eastern Mount Tai, the malady is one.
translations.idiomatic: I have watched commandery generals fail for decades—from Bird-and-Rat to Mount Tai, the disease is the same.

sentences.zh: 力求猛敵，不如清平；

translations.literal: Striving to seek fierce enemies is not as good as clarity and peace;
translations.idiomatic: Seeking fierce enemies is inferior to restoring order;

sentences.zh: 勤明孫、吳，未若奉法。

translations.literal: Diligently mastering Sun and Wu is not equal to upholding the law.
translations.idiomatic: Mastering Sunzi and Wuzi is less than upholding the law.

sentences.zh: 前變未遠，臣誠戚之，是以越職盡其區區。

translations.literal: The prior disaster is not distant; your servant is truly grieved, and therefore oversteps office to exhaust my humble effort.
translations.idiomatic: The last disaster is still fresh; grieved, I overstep my office to offer what little I can.

sentences.zh: 」詔以規為中郎將，持節監關西兵討零吾等。

translations.literal: 」An edict appointed Gui as General of the Gentlemen of the Palace, bearing the staff to oversee Guanxi troops in campaigning against Lingwu and others.
translations.idiomatic: 」An edict made Gui General of the Gentlemen of the Palace with staff authority to command Guanxi troops against Lingwu and others.

sentences.zh: 十一月，規擊羌，破之，斬首八百級。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Gui attacked the Qiang, defeated them, and took eight hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Gui attacked the Qiang, routed them, and took eight hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 先零諸種羌慕規威信，相勸降者十餘萬。

translations.literal: Various Xianling Qiang tribes admired Gui's authority and trustworthiness; those who urged one another to surrender numbered more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xianling Qiang tribes, admiring Gui's authority, surrendered in numbers exceeding one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬午，南宮丙署火。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day renwu, the Bing Office of the Southern Palace burned.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on renwu day, the Bing Office of the Southern Palace burned.

sentences.zh: 三月，沈氐羌寇張掖、酒泉。

translations.literal: In the third month, Shenshi Qiang raided Zhangye and Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Shenshi Qiang raided Zhangye and Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 皇甫規發先零諸種羌，共討隴右，而道路隔絕，軍中大疫，死者十三四。

translations.literal: Huangfu Gui mobilized various Xianling Qiang tribes to campaign jointly in Longyou, but roads were cut off and a great pestilence struck the army—three or four in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Gui mobilized Xianling Qiang to campaign in Longyou, but roads were cut and pestilence swept the army—three or four in ten died.

sentences.zh: 規親入庵廬，巡視將士，三軍感悅。

translations.literal: Gui personally entered the tents and huts and inspected officers and soldiers; the three armies were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Gui walked the camps himself to visit the troops; the army was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 東羌遂遣使乞降，涼州復通。

translations.literal: The Eastern Qiang then sent envoys begging to surrender, and Liang Province was open again.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Qiang sent envoys to surrender, and Liang Province was reachable again.

sentences.zh: 先是安定太守孫俊受取狼藉，屬國都尉李翕、督軍御史張稟多殺降羌，涼州刺史郭閎、漢陽太守趙熹並老弱不任職，而皆倚恃權貴，不遵法度。

translations.literal: Earlier, Administrator of Anding Sun Jun's takings were in utter disorder; Dependent State Commandant Li Xi and Supervising Army Imperial Secretary Zhang Bing killed many surrendered Qiang; Liang Province Inspector Guo Hong and Administrator of Hanyang Zhao Xi were both aged and weak and unfit for office, yet all relied on powerful patrons and did not observe the law.
translations.idiomatic: Anding Administrator Sun Jun had embezzled freely; Dependent State Commandant Li Xi and Supervising Army Censor Zhang Bing slaughtered surrendered Qiang; Liang Inspector Guo Hong and Hanyang Administrator Zhao Xi were old, weak, and unfit—yet all leaned on powerful patrons and flouted the law.

sentences.zh: 規到，悉條奏其罪，或免或誅。

translations.literal: When Gui arrived, he memorialized all their crimes in detail; some were dismissed, some executed.
translations.idiomatic: Gui arrived, listed all their crimes, and had some dismissed and some executed.

sentences.zh: 羌人聞之，翕然反善，沈氐大豪滇昌、饑恬等十餘萬口復詣規降。

translations.literal: When the Qiang heard of it, they all at once turned to goodness. Shenshi grand chiefs Dianchang, Jitian, and others—more than one hundred thousand—again came to Gui to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang heard and turned toward peace. Shenshi chiefs Dianchang, Jitian, and others—more than one hundred thousand—surrendered to Gui.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，長沙賊起，寇桂陽、蒼梧。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Changsha bandits rose and raided Guiyang and Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Changsha rebels raided Guiyang and Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，恭陵東闕火。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, the eastern gate-tower of Gongling burned.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day, the eastern gate-tower of Gongling burned.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，虎賁掖門火。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, the Tiger Guard side gate burned.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day, the Tiger Guard side gate burned.

sentences.zh: 五月，康陵園寢火。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the park tomb of Kangling burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the park tomb of Kangling burned.

sentences.zh: 長沙、零陵賊入桂陽、蒼梧、南海，交趾刺史及蒼梧太守望風逃奔，遣御史中丞盛修督州郡募兵討之，不能克。

translations.literal: Changsha and Lingling bandits entered Guiyang, Cangwu, and Nanhai. The Inspector of Jiaozhi and Administrator of Cangwu fled at the wind of their coming. Imperial Secretary and Palace Assistant Sheng Xiu was sent to oversee the provinces and commanderies in raising troops to campaign against them, but could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha and Lingling rebels overran Guiyang, Cangwu, and Nanhai. The Jiaozhi Inspector and Cangwu Administrator fled. Censor Sheng Xiu was sent to raise troops but could not defeat them.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，京師地震。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, the capital was shaken by earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day, the capital was shaken by earthquake.

sentences.zh: 甲申，中藏府丞祿署火。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, the Lu Office of the Palace Storehouse Director burned.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day, the Lu Office of the Palace Storehouse burned.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己未，南宮承善闥火。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jiwei, the Chenshan Gate of the Southern Palace burned.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jiwei day, the Chenshan Gate of the Southern Palace burned.

sentences.zh: 鳥吾羌寇漢陽，隴西、金城諸郡兵討破之。

translations.literal: Wuwu Qiang raided Hanyang; troops of Longxi, Jincheng, and other commanderies campaigned against and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwu Qiang raided Hanyang; troops from Longxi, Jincheng, and neighboring commanderies defeated them.

sentences.zh: 艾縣賊攻長沙郡縣，殺益陽令，眾至萬餘人；

translations.literal: Bandits of Ai County attacked the counties of Changsha, killed the magistrate of Yiyang, and numbered more than ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Ai County rebels attacked Changsha counties, killed the magistrate of Yiyang, and swelled to more than ten thousand;

sentences.zh: 謁者馬睦督荊州刺史劉度擊之，軍敗，睦、度奔走。

translations.literal: Usher Ma Mu supervised Jing Province Inspector Liu Du in attacking them. The army was defeated; Mu and Du fled.
translations.idiomatic: Usher Ma Mu supervised Jing Inspector Liu Du against them. The army was routed; Mu and Du fled.

sentences.zh: 零陵蠻亦反。

translations.literal: Lingling Man also rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Lingling tribes rebelled as well.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，武陵蠻反，寇江陵，南郡太守李肅奔走，主簿胡爽扣馬首諫曰：「蠻夷見郡無儆備，故敢乘間而進。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Wuling Man rebelled and raided Jiangling. Administrator of Nanjun Li Su fled. Chief Clerk Hu Shuang seized the horse's head and remonstrated: "The Man and Yi see the commandery without precaution, therefore dare seize the interval to advance.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Wuling tribes rebelled and raided Jiangling. Nanjun Administrator Li Su fled. Chief Clerk Hu Shuang grabbed his bridle and remonstrated: "The tribes saw the commandery undefended and seized the moment to attack.

sentences.zh: 明府為國大臣，連城千里，舉旗鳴鼓，應聲十萬，奈何委符守之重，而為逋逃之人乎！

translations.literal: Your Excellency is a great minister of the state; your chained cities stretch a thousand li—raise the banner and beat the drum and one hundred thousand will answer. How can you abandon the weight of the tally and seal of guardianship and become a fugitive!
translations.idiomatic: You are a great minister of the state; your cities stretch a thousand li—raise banner and drum and a hundred thousand will answer. How can you abandon your charge and flee!

sentences.zh: 」肅拔刃向爽曰：「掾促去！

translations.literal: 」Su drew his blade toward Shuang and said: "Clerk, hurry away!
translations.idiomatic: 」Su drew his blade on Shuang: "Clerk, get out of my way!

sentences.zh: 太守今急，何暇此計！

translations.literal: The Administrator is urgent now—what leisure for this scheme!
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator is in peril—no time for this!

sentences.zh: 」爽抱馬固諫，肅遂殺爽而走。

translations.literal: 」Shuang clung to the horse and firmly remonstrated. Su then killed Shuang and fled.
translations.idiomatic: 」Shuang clung to the bridle and remonstrated still. Su killed him and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，征肅，棄市；

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of it, summoned Su, and had him executed in the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard, summoned Su, and executed him in the marketplace;

sentences.zh: 度、睦減死一等；

translations.literal: Du and Mu had their death sentences reduced one degree;
translations.idiomatic: Du and Mu had their sentences reduced one degree from death;

sentences.zh: 復爽門閭，拜家一人為郎。

translations.literal: Shuang's gate and lane were restored; one man of his family was appointed Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's household honors were restored; one family member was appointed Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 尚書朱穆舉右校令山陽度尚為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Zhu Mu recommended Colonel of the Right Du Shang of Shanyang as Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhu Mu recommended Colonel of the Right Du Shang of Shanyang as Jing Inspector.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以太常馮緄為車騎將軍，將兵十餘萬討武陵蠻。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Grand Master of Ceremonies Feng Gun was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, leading more than one hundred thousand troops to campaign against Wuling Man.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day, Grand Master of Ceremonies Feng Gun was made General of Chariots and Cavalry at the head of more than one hundred thousand men against the Wuling tribes.

sentences.zh: 先是，所遣將帥，宦官多陷以折耗軍資，往往抵罪，緄願請中常侍一人監軍財費。

translations.literal: Earlier, of generals dispatched, eunuchs often trapped them on charges of wasting military supplies, and they often paid with their lives. Gun wished to request one Palace Attendant to oversee military finances.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier eunuchs often framed dispatched generals for wasting supplies; many paid with their lives. Gun asked for a Palace Attendant to oversee military funds.

sentences.zh: 尚書朱穆奏「緄以財自嫌，失大臣之節；

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Zhu Mu memorialized: "Gun, through suspicion over finances, has lost a great minister's integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhu Mu memorialized: "Gun's suspicion over finances betrays a great minister's integrity;

sentences.zh: 」有詔勿劾。

translations.literal: 」An edict said not to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: 」An edict ordered that he not be impeached.

sentences.zh: 緄請前武陵太守應奉與俱，拜從事中郎。

translations.literal: Gun requested former Administrator of Wuling Ying Feng to go with him and appointed him Attendant of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Gun asked former Wuling Administrator Ying Feng to accompany him and made him Attendant of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 十一月，緄軍至長沙，賊聞之，悉詣營乞降。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Gun's army reached Changsha. When the bandits heard, they all came to the camp to beg surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Gun reached Changsha. The rebels heard and came to his camp to surrender.

sentences.zh: 進擊武陵蠻夷，斬首四千餘級，受降十餘萬人，荊州平定。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Wuling Man and Yi, he took more than four thousand heads and accepted the surrender of more than one hundred thousand people. Jing Province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against the Wuling tribes, took more than four thousand heads, accepted more than one hundred thousand surrenders, and pacified Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 詔書賜錢一億，固讓不受，振旅還京師，推功於應奉，薦以為司隸校尉；

translations.literal: An edict granted one hundred million cash. He firmly declined and would not accept. He returned the army to the capital, credited Ying Feng with the merit, and recommended him as Colonel of the Masters of Writing in the Capital;
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him one hundred million cash. He refused. He returned to the capital, credited Ying Feng, and recommended him as Metropolitan Colonel;

sentences.zh: 而上書乞骸骨，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial begging to retire on account of old bones; the court did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to retire; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 滇那羌寇武威、張掖、酒泉。

translations.literal: Dianna Qiang raided Wuwei, Zhangye, and Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Dianna Qiang raided Wuwei, Zhangye, and Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 太尉劉矩免，以太常楊秉為太尉。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Liu Ju was dismissed; Grand Master of Ceremonies Yang Bing was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Liu Ju was dismissed and Grand Master of Ceremonies Yang Bing appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 皇甫規持節為將，還督鄉里，既無它私惠，而多所舉奏，又惡絕宦官，不與交通。

translations.literal: Huangfu Gui, bearing the staff as general, returned to oversee his home district. He offered no other private favors, yet memorialized many impeachments, and hated and cut off eunuchs, having no dealings with them.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Gui, staff-bearing general in his home country, granted no private favors but impeached widely, shunned eunuchs, and would not deal with them.

sentences.zh: 於是中外並怨，遂共誣規貨賂群羌，令其文降，帝璽書誚讓相屬。

translations.literal: Thereupon inner and outer courts alike resented him. They jointly slandered Gui for bribing the Qiang tribes to make a show of surrender. Imperial sealed letters of rebuke followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Court and camp alike resented him. They jointly accused Gui of bribing Qiang tribes into sham surrender. Imperial rebukes arrived in succession.

sentences.zh: 規上書自訟曰：「四年之秋，戎丑蠢戾，舊都懼駭，朝廷西顧。

translations.literal: Gui submitted a memorial pleading his own case, saying: "In the autumn of the fourth year, the Rong tribes grew savage and rebellious; the old capital feared and was shaken; the court looked west with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Gui pleaded his case: "In the autumn of the fourth year, barbarians rebelled; the old capital trembled; the court looked west in alarm.

sentences.zh: 臣振國威靈，羌戎稽首，所省之費一億以上。

translations.literal: Your servant raised the state's authority and numen; Qiang and Rong bowed their heads. Expenses saved amounted to more than one hundred million.
translations.idiomatic: I raised the state's authority; Qiang and Rong submitted. I saved more than one hundred million in costs.

sentences.zh: 以為忠臣之義不敢告勞，故恥以片言自及微效，然比方先事，庶免罪悔。

translations.literal: Thinking that a loyal minister's duty dares not speak of toil, I was ashamed to mention in a word my slight achievement; yet comparing with prior affairs, I hope to escape guilt and regret.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal minister does not boast of toil, and I was ashamed to mention my small service—yet compared with what came before, I hoped to avoid reproach.

sentences.zh: 前踐州界，先奏孫俊、李翕、張稟；

translations.literal: Earlier, upon entering the province, I first memorialized against Sun Jun, Li Xi, and Zhang Bing;
translations.idiomatic: Entering the province, I first impeached Sun Jun, Li Xi, and Zhang Bing;

sentences.zh: 旋師南征，又上郭閎、趙熹，陳其過惡，執據大辟。

translations.literal: Turning the army south to campaign, I again memorialized against Guo Hong and Zhao Xi, stating their crimes and insisting on the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign I impeached Guo Hong and Zhao Xi, detailing their crimes and demanding execution.

sentences.zh: 凡此五臣，支黨半國，其餘墨綬下至小吏，所連及者復有百餘。

translations.literal: These five ministers in all—their factions and partisans half the state; besides them, from black-cord officials down to petty clerks, those implicated numbered more than one hundred again.
translations.idiomatic: These five officials commanded factions across half the realm; more than a hundred lesser officials were implicated besides.

sentences.zh: 吏托報將之怨，子思復父之恥，載贄馳車，懷糧步走，交構豪門，競流謗讟，雲臣私報諸羌，讎以錢貨。

translations.literal: Officials borrowed generals' grudges to repay; sons thought to avenge fathers' shame. Bearing gifts they drove chariots; carrying rations they walked. They wove plots with great houses and competed in spreading slander, saying your servant privately repaid the Qiang tribes and rewarded them with money and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Officials nursed grudges against generals; sons sought to avenge fathers. They rode with gifts and walked with provisions, conspiring with great houses to spread slander—that I privately paid the Qiang with money.

sentences.zh: 若臣以私財，則家無擔石；

translations.literal: If your servant used private wealth, my household has not a single stone of grain;
translations.idiomatic: If I used private wealth, my home holds not a stone of grain;

sentences.zh: 如物出於官，則文簿易考。

translations.literal: If goods came from the office, documents and ledgers are easy to examine.
translations.idiomatic: If public funds were used, the ledgers can be checked.

sentences.zh: 就臣愚惑，信如言者，前世尚遺匈奴以宮姬，鎮烏孫以公主；

translations.literal: Grant your servant's dull confusion: if one truly believes such words, in former ages the court still sent palace women to the Xiongnu and stationed princesses to pacify Wusun;
translations.idiomatic: Even if you believe them: past dynasties sent palace women to the Xiongnu and princesses to Wusun;

sentences.zh: 今臣但費千萬以懷叛羌，則良臣之才略，兵家之所貴，將有何罪負義違理乎！

translations.literal: If today your servant merely spent tens of millions to win over rebellious Qiang, then what crime of betraying righteousness and violating reason would a good minister's talent and strategy—the very thing military families prize—carry!
translations.idiomatic: If spending tens of millions to win rebellious Qiang is crime, then what offense lies in the talent and strategy armies prize!

sentences.zh: 自永初以來，將出不少，覆軍有五，動資巨億，有旋車完封，寫之權門，而名成功立，厚加爵封。

translations.literal: Since the Yongchu era, generals dispatched have not been few; armies destroyed number five; resources mobilized reach hundreds of millions. Some returned with chariots intact and seals unbroken, copied their accounts to powerful gates, yet fame and success were established and thick ranks and enfeoffments added.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yongchu, many generals marched; five armies were destroyed; billions were spent. Some returned with chariots intact, falsified accounts for powerful patrons—and won fame, titles, and thick rewards.

sentences.zh: 今臣還督本土，糾舉諸郡，絕交離親，戮辱舊故，眾謗陰害，固其宜也！

translations.literal: Now your servant returns to oversee native soil, impeaches across commanderies, severs ties and estranges kin, shames old associates—public slander and hidden harm are surely fitting!
translations.idiomatic: I returned home, impeached across the commanderies, severed ties and shamed old associates—of course they slander and plot against me!

sentences.zh: 帝乃征規還，拜議郎，論功當封；

translations.literal: The Emperor then summoned Gui back and appointed him Gentleman Consultant; by merit he ought to have been enfeoffed;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor recalled Gui, made him Gentleman Consultant, and judged his merit worthy of enfeoffment;

sentences.zh: 而中常侍徐璜、左心官欲從求貨，數遣賓客就問功狀，規終不答。

translations.literal: But Palace Attendants Xu Huang and Zuo Xinguan wished to extort goods from him and repeatedly sent clients to inquire about his achievements; Gui ultimately would not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendants Xu Huang and Zuo Xinguan tried to extort him, sending clients repeatedly to discuss his merit; Gui refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 璜等忿怒，陷以前事，下之於吏。

translations.literal: Huang and the others were enraged, trapped him with the prior matter, and handed him to the judicial officers.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they framed him on the old charge and handed him to the courts.

sentences.zh: 官屬欲賦斂請謝，規誓而不聽，遂以餘寇不絕，坐系廷尉，論輸左校。

translations.literal: His staff wished to levy funds to plead for pardon; Gui swore and would not listen. He was then convicted because remnant raiders were unceasing, imprisoned by the Commandant of Justice, and sentenced to the Left Construction Corps.
translations.idiomatic: His staff wanted to raise funds to buy pardon; Gui refused. Convicted because raids continued, he was imprisoned and sentenced to the Left Construction Corps.

sentences.zh: 諸公及太學生張鳳等三百餘人詣闕訟之，會赦，歸家。

translations.literal: Various Excellencies and Imperial University student Zhang Feng and more than three hundred others went to the palace gate to plead his case. They met an amnesty and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Excellencies and more than three hundred students led by Zhang Feng petitioned at the palace gate. An amnesty came; Gui went home.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，戊午，司徒種暠薨。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on the day wuwu, Minister over the Masses Zhong Hao died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, on wuwu day, Minister over the Masses Zhong Hao died.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊戌，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day wuxu, there was an amnesty for all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuxu day, an empire-wide amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 以衛尉穎川許栩為司徒。

translations.literal: Minister of the Guards Xu Xu of Yingchuan was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Guards Xu Xu of Yingchuan was made Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛亥，康陵東署火。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day xinhai, the eastern office of Kangling burned.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on xinhai day, the eastern office of Kangling burned.

sentences.zh: 五月，鮮卑寇遼東屬國。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Xianbei raided the Dependent State of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Xianbei raided the Liaodong Dependent State.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲申，平陵園寢火。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jiashen, the park tomb of Pingling burned.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jiashen day, the park tomb of Pingling burned.

sentences.zh: 桂陽賊李研等寇郡界，武陵蠻復反。

translations.literal: Guiyang bandits Li Yan and others raided the commandery borders; Wuling Man rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang rebels Li Yan and others raided the borders; the Wuling tribes rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 太守陳奉討平之。

translations.literal: Administrator Chen Feng campaigned against and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Chen Feng suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 宦官素惡馮緄，八月，緄坐軍還盜賊復發，免。

translations.literal: Eunuchs had long hated Feng Gun. In the eighth month, Gun was convicted because after the army returned bandits rose again, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs long hated Feng Gun. In the eighth month he was dismissed because bandits rose again after his army returned.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙辰，上校獵廣成，遂幸函谷關、上林苑。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day bingchen, the Emperor hunted at Guangcheng, then traveled in state to Hangu Pass and the Shanglin Park.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on bingchen day, the Emperor hunted at Guangcheng, then visited Hangu Pass and the Shanglin Park.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳陳蕃上疏諫曰：「安平之時，游畋宜有節，況今有三空之厄哉！

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Luminaries Chen Fan submitted a remonstrance, saying: "In times of peace and stability, hunting and sport ought to have limits—how much more now when there is the calamity of the Three Empties!
translations.idiomatic: Director Chen Fan remonstrated: "Even in peaceful times hunting should be restrained—how much more now, in the calamity of the Three Empties!

sentences.zh: 田野空，朝廷空，倉庫空。

translations.literal: The fields are empty, the court is empty, the storehouses are empty.
translations.idiomatic: The fields are empty, the court is empty, the treasuries are empty.

sentences.zh: 加之兵戎未戢，四方離散，是陛下焦心毀顏，坐以待旦之時也，豈宜揚旗曜武，騁心輿馬之觀乎！

translations.literal: Added to this, arms are not yet stilled and the four quarters are scattered. This is the time when Your Majesty should be anxious in heart and haggard in face, sitting upright awaiting dawn—how can it be fitting to raise banners and display martial glory, giving rein to heart and chariot-and-horse spectacles!
translations.idiomatic: Arms are not stilled; the realm is scattered. This is when you should sit anxious awaiting dawn—how can you raise banners for sport and chase after chariots and horses!

sentences.zh: 又前秋多雨，民始種麥，今失其勸種之時，而令給驅禽除路之役，非賢聖恤民之意也。

translations.literal: Moreover, last autumn rains were heavy; the people had just begun to plant wheat. Now the season for encouraging planting is lost, yet they are ordered to serve in driving game and clearing roads—this is not the intent of sage and worthy in cherishing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Last autumn's rains were heavy; farmers had just sown wheat. Now planting season is lost, yet you command them to clear roads for the hunt—this is not how sages cherish the people.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，不納。

translations.literal: 」The memorial was submitted and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: 」The memorial was ignored.

sentences.zh: 十一月，司空劉寵免。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Minister of Works Liu Chong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Minister of Works Liu Chong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以衛尉周景為司空。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Minister of the Guards Zhou Jing was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Minister of the Guards Zhou Jing was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 景，榮之孫也。

translations.literal: Jing was the grandson of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was the grandson of Rong.

sentences.zh: 時宦官方熾，景與太尉楊秉上言：「內外吏職，多非其人。

translations.literal: At this time eunuch power was blazing. Jing together with Grand Commandant Yang Bing submitted a statement: "Inner and outer official posts—many are not held by the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch power was at its height. Jing and Grand Commandant Yang Bing submitted: "Many inner and outer offices are held by unworthy men.

sentences.zh: 舊典，中臣子弟，不得居位秉勢；

translations.literal: By old statute, sons and younger brothers of inner ministers may not hold office and wield influence;
translations.idiomatic: By ancient statute, eunuchs' kin could not hold office or power;

sentences.zh: 而今枝葉賓客，布列職署，或年少庸人，典據守宰；

translations.literal: Yet today branches, leaves, clients, and guests fill the offices; some are young and mediocre men who hold and govern as administrators and chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Today their kin and clients fill every office—some young mediocrities governing provinces and commanderies;

sentences.zh: 上下忿患，四方愁毒。

translations.literal: Superiors and inferiors resent and suffer; the four quarters grieve and are poisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Above and below seethe with resentment; the four quarters groan under poison.

sentences.zh: 可遵用舊章，退貪殘，塞災謗。

translations.literal: One may follow the old statutes, dismiss the greedy and cruel, and stop calamity and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the old statutes: dismiss the greedy and cruel; stop the calamities and slander.

sentences.zh: 請下司隸校尉、中二千石、城門、五營校尉、北軍中候，各實核所部；

translations.literal: We request that orders be sent to the Colonel of the Masters of Writing in the Capital, grandees of two thousand bushels, gate commanders, colonels of the five camps, and the Commandant of the Northern Army to verify their jurisdictions;
translations.idiomatic: Order the Metropolitan Colonel, two-thousand-bushel officials, gate commanders, colonels of the five camps, and Northern Army commandants to audit their jurisdictions;

sentences.zh: 應當斥罷，自以狀言三府，兼察有遺漏，續上。

translations.literal: Those who should be dismissed and cast out should report in detail to the Three Excellencies, and also investigate for omissions and continue submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Those who should be dismissed should report to the Three Excellencies; investigate omissions and continue reporting.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是秉條奏牧、守、青州刺史羊亮等五十餘人，或死或免，天下莫不肅然。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bing memorialized in detail governors, administrators, Inspector of Qing Province Yang Liang, and more than fifty others—some were executed, some dismissed—and all under heaven was awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: Bing then listed more than fifty governors, administrators, and officials including Qing Inspector Yang Liang—some executed, some dismissed—and the realm stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 詔征皇甫規為度遼將軍。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Huangfu Gui as General Who Crosses the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Huangfu Gui as General Who Crosses the Liao.

sentences.zh: 初，張奐坐梁冀故吏，免官禁錮，凡諸交舊，莫敢為言；

translations.literal: Initially, Zhang Huan, convicted as a former clerk of Liang Ji, was dismissed from office and forbidden from holding office. Of all associates and old friends, none dared speak for him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan, implicated as a former Liang Ji clerk, was dismissed and barred from office. No friend or associate dared speak for him;

sentences.zh: 唯規薦舉，前後七上，由是拜武威太守。

translations.literal: Only Gui recommended and nominated him, memorializing seven times in succession, whereby he was appointed Administrator of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gui recommended him—seven memorials in succession—until he was appointed Administrator of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 及規為度遼，到營數月，上書薦奐，「才略兼優，宜正元帥，以從眾望。

translations.literal: When Gui became General Who Crosses the Liao, after several months at camp he submitted a memorial recommending Huan: "Talent and strategy both excellent—he should be made supreme commander to accord with public expectation.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui became General Who Crosses the Liao, after months in camp he recommended Huan: "His talent and strategy excel; he should command to meet the people's hopes.

sentences.zh: 若猶謂愚臣宜充舉事者，願乞冗官，以為奐副。

translations.literal: If you still think your foolish servant should fill the role of conducting affairs, I beg a supernumerary post to serve as Huan's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: If you still want me in the field, give me a humble post as Huan's deputy.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之。

translations.literal: 」The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: 」The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 以奐代規為度遼將軍，以規為使匈奴中郎將。

translations.literal: Huan replaced Gui as General Who Crosses the Liao; Gui was made General of the Gentlemen of the Palace Acting as Emissary to the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan replaced Gui as General Who Crosses the Liao; Gui became Emissary General to the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 西州吏民守闕為前護羌校尉段熲訟冤者甚眾，會滇那等諸種羌益熾，涼州幾亡，乃復以熲為護羌校尉。

translations.literal: Officials and people of the western provinces guarding the palace gate to plead the injustice of former Protector of the Qiang Duan Yong were very numerous. As Dianna and various Qiang tribes grew still fiercer and Liang Province nearly perished, Yong was again made Protector of the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Western officials and people thronged the palace gate to plead Duan Yong's innocence. As Dianna Qiang grew fiercer and Liang Province nearly fell, Yong was restored as Protector of the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 尚書朱穆疾宦官恣橫，上疏曰：「按漢故事，中常侍參選士人，建武以後，乃悉用宦者。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Zhu Mu, grieved that eunuchs were wilful and overbearing, submitted a memorial: "According to Han precedent, Palace Attendants were chosen from among scholars; after Jianwu, all were eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhu Mu, appalled by eunuch arrogance, memorialized: "By Han precedent, Palace Attendants were chosen from scholars; after Jianwu, all were eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 自延平以來，浸益貴盛，假貂璫之飾，處常伯之任，天朝政事，一更其手。

translations.literal: From Yanping onward they gradually grew ever more honored and powerful, borrowing regalia of sable and ring, holding posts of constant lords—court governance of the celestial dynasty changed entirely at their hands.
translations.idiomatic: From Yanping they grew ever grander, wearing sable regalia, holding chief posts—court governance passed entirely into their hands.

sentences.zh: 權傾海內，寵貴無極，子弟親戚，並荷榮任。

translations.literal: Power tilted across the seas; favor and honor knew no limit; sons, younger brothers, and kin all bore glorious appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Their power tilted the realm; honor knew no limit; kin of every degree held glorious posts.

sentences.zh: 放濫驕溢，莫能禁御，窮破天下，空竭小民。

translations.literal: Licentious, arrogant, and overflowing, none could restrain them. They exhausted and broke the realm and emptied and drained the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Licentious and arrogant beyond restraint, they beggared the realm and drained the people dry.

sentences.zh: 愚臣以為可悉罷省，遵復往初，更選海內清淳之士明達國體者，以補其處，即兆庶黎萌，蒙被聖化矣！

translations.literal: Your foolish servant thinks they may all be dismissed and abolished, returning to former beginnings, and that pure and honest men within the seas who understand the state's form may be newly selected to fill those posts—then the myriad common folk and budding people would receive sage transformation!
translations.idiomatic: I believe they should all be abolished; restore the old ways; appoint pure, capable men from across the realm—and the people would receive true sage rule!

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 後穆因進見，復口陳曰：「臣聞漢家舊典，置侍中、中常侍各一人，省尚書事；

translations.literal: Later Mu, on entering audience, again stated orally: "Your servant has heard the old statutes of the house of Han: one Palace Attendant and one Regular Palace Attendant were set, overseeing Masters of Writing affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Later, on audience, Mu spoke again: "I have heard the old Han statutes: one Attendant and one Regular Attendant oversaw the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎一人，傳發書奏；

translations.literal: one Gentleman of the Yellow Gates transmitted and issued memorials;
translations.idiomatic: one Gentleman of the Yellow Gates transmitted memorials;

sentences.zh: 皆用姓族。

translations.literal: all were drawn from surname clans.
translations.idiomatic: all were drawn from established families.

sentences.zh: 自和熹太后以女主稱制，不接公卿，乃以閹人為常侍，小黃門通命兩宮。

translations.literal: From Empress Dowager Hexi ruling as female sovereign, not receiving the Three Excellencies, eunuchs were made Regular Attendants and Junior Palace Attendants communicated orders between the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Hexi ruled as regent and refused the Three Excellencies, eunuchs became Regular Attendants and Junior Attendants carried orders between the palaces.

sentences.zh: 自此以來，權傾人主，窮困天下，宜皆罷遣，博選耆儒宿德，與參政事。

translations.literal: From this time power tilted against the sovereign and exhausted the realm. They ought all to be dismissed and sent away; broadly select aged Confucians of long virtue to participate in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Since then power has tilted against the throne and exhausted the realm. Dismiss them all; choose aged Confucians of proven virtue to govern.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，不應。

translations.literal: 」The Emperor was angry and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Emperor raged and did not answer.

sentences.zh: 穆伏不肯起，左右傳「出！

translations.literal: Mu prostrated himself and would not rise. Attendants transmitted: "Withdraw!
translations.idiomatic: Mu prostrated himself and would not rise. Attendants called: "Withdraw!

sentences.zh: 」良久，乃趨而去。

translations.literal: 」After a long while he hurried away.
translations.idiomatic: 」After a long while he hurried away.

sentences.zh: 自此中官數因事稱詔詆毀之。

translations.literal: From this time the inner officials repeatedly used affairs as pretexts to proclaim edicts slandering him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on eunuchs repeatedly issued edicts slandering him.

sentences.zh: 穆素剛，不得意，居無幾，憤懣發疽卒。

translations.literal: Mu was by nature stern; not getting his way, after not long in residence he died of an abscess brought on by indignant frustration.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was by nature stern. Frustrated, he soon died of an abscess born of rage.
